Housed in the Vieux-Château de Laval, the birthplace of Douanier Rousseau, it presents the modern primitives — Rousseau, Séraphine de Senlis, André Bauchant — and outsider art.

marq-musee-d-art-roger-quilliot.name: Roger-Quilliot Art Museum
marq-musee-d-art-roger-quilliot.description: Museum opened in 1992 in part of the former Ursuline convent, built in the 17th century in the Montferrand district. It unfolds a chronological trail from the Middle Ages, with its Romanesque sculptures and Auvergne Virgins in Majesty, to the 20th century, with paintings by Philippe de Champaigne, Boucher and Vernet.

memorial-ascq-1944.name: Ascq 1944 Memorial
memorial-ascq-1944.description: Memorial devoted to the Ascq massacre, in which SS troops of the Hitlerjugend division executed eighty-six civilians on the night of 1-2 April 1944 in reprisal for a railway sabotage. Housed in the former infant welfare clinic, opened in 1984 and redesigned in 2005, it broadens its scope to the violence of the war and the post-war trials.

memorial-de-l-internement-et-de-la-depor.name: Memorial of Internment and Deportation — Royallieu Camp
memorial-de-l-internement-et-de-la-depor.description: Memorial set up in three buildings of the former Royallieu barracks, which the German occupiers turned into an internment and transit camp, Frontstalag 122, from June 1941 to August 1944. More than 54,000 people were interned there — Resistance fighters, Jews, Roma, hostages and foreigners — before being deported; the memorial was inaugurated in February 2008.

memorial-de-la-marseillaise.name: Memorial of La Marseillaise
memorial-de-la-marseillaise.description: Memorial set up on rue Thubaneau, in the former jeu de paume court that housed the Marseille Jacobin club. It was there that the Marseille federated volunteers struck up, in 1792, Rouget de Lisle's Chant de guerre pour l'armée du Rhin, which they carried to Paris and which became La Marseillaise; an immersive trail retraces its history.

memorial-de-la-shoah.name: Shoah Memorial
memorial-de-la-shoah.description: France's central Holocaust memorial and museum, in the Marais. The Wall of Names lists the 76,000 Jews deported from France, while a permanent exhibition and a major documentation centre trace the Shoah and Jewish life in Europe.

memorial-de-la-shoah-de-drancy.name: Drancy Shoah Memorial
memorial-de-la-shoah-de-drancy.description: Memorial and museum opened in 2012 facing the Cité de la Muette, the housing estate that served as the Drancy internment camp from 1941 to 1944, from which some 63,000 Jews were deported. Its exhibition documents the camp's history and daily life.

memorial-des-deportations.name: Memorial of the Deportations
memorial-des-deportations.description: Memorial opened in December 2019 in a bunker built by the German army at the foot of Fort Saint-Jean in Marseille. Across three levels, it traces the repression and persecution of the Occupation: the round-ups of January 1943, the destruction of the old districts, and the deportation of residents who were arrested.

miam-musee-international-des-arts-modest.name: MIAM — International Museum of Modest Art
miam-musee-international-des-arts-modest.description: Founded in 2000 by the Sète-born artist Hervé Di Rosa and the collector Bernard Belluc, the MIAM occupies a former wine warehouse redesigned by the architect Patrick Bouchain. It champions "modest art": toys, figurines, manufactured or homemade objects, at the crossroads of art brut, naive art and popular art.

mo-co-hotel-des-collections.name: MO.CO. Hôtel des Collections
mo-co-hotel-des-collections.description: Exhibition venue opened in June 2019 in the Hôtel Montcalm, a 19th-century mansion restored and extended with a new wing in the heart of Montpellier. The flagship venue of MO.CO., it holds no collection of its own, presenting across more than 3,000 square metres groups of works borrowed from public and private collections around the world.

mo-co-panacee.name: MO.CO. Panacée
mo-co-panacee.description: Contemporary art centre opened in 2013 in Montpellier's former royal college of medicine, a building with a courtyard and galleries restored for exhibitions. Since 2017 one of the three venues of MO.CO. Montpellier Contemporain, alongside the school of fine arts and the Hôtel des Collections, it programmes exhibitions, residencies and emerging creation.

monastere-de-saorge.name: Monastery of Saorge
monastere-de-saorge.description: Franciscan monastery founded in 1633 above the hilltop village of Saorge, in the upper Roya valley. Its four-gallery cloister preserves 18th-century frescoes depicting the life of Saint Francis, and the monastery, bought by the state in 1967, has hosted a writers' residency since 2001.

monastere-royal-de-brou-a-bourg-en-bress.name: Royal Monastery of Brou, Bourg-en-Bresse
monastere-royal-de-brou-a-bourg-en-bress.description: Monastic complex built from 1506 by Margaret of Austria to house the tomb of her husband Philibert the Fair, in the Flamboyant Gothic style of Brabant architect Louis van Bodeghem. The church of Saint-Nicolas-de-Tolentin holds the sculpted tombs of Margaret of Austria, Philibert the Fair and Margaret of Bourbon, while the three cloisters now house the Musée de Brou.

moulin-de-la-blies-musee-des-techniques-.name: Moulin de la Blies — Museum of Faience-Making Techniques
moulin-de-la-blies-musee-des-techniques-.description: Former mill for grinding raw materials for the Sarreguemines faience works, built in 1841 by Alexandre de Geiger and in operation until 1969. Bought by the town in 1990 and opened to the public in 1998, it displays the machinery and workshops of faience-making, extended since 2009 by a faience-makers' garden.

muba-eugene-leroy.name: MUba Eugène-Leroy
muba-eugene-leroy.description: Tourcoing's museum of fine arts, created around 1860 and housed since 1931 in the Hôtel Roussel-Defontaine, a mansion built in 1866. It took its current name in 2009, after his heirs donated nearly six hundred works by the Tourcoing painter Eugène Leroy, which are shown alongside an older collection that includes a Rembrandt.

mucem.name: Museum of European and Mediterranean Civilisations
mucem.description: National museum of society devoted to the anthropology of the European and Mediterranean worlds, inaugurated in 2013 when Marseille was European Capital of Culture. It occupies, at the entrance to the Vieux-Port, a building by Rudy Ricciotti, linked by footbridge to Fort Saint-Jean, and inherited the collections of the former National Museum of Popular Arts and Traditions.

mudo-musee-de-l-oise.name: MUDO — Oise Departmental Museum
mudo-musee-de-l-oise.description: The departmental museum occupies the former episcopal palace of Beauvais, built from as early as the 12th century on the Gallo-Roman ramparts, fitted with a fortified gatehouse in the 14th century and later rebuilt in the Renaissance. Opened in 1981, it displays medieval sculpture, old master painting, ceramics and a 19th-century collection featuring Corot and Sisley.

muma-musee-d-art-moderne-andre-malraux.name: MuMa — André Malraux Museum of Modern Art
muma-musee-d-art-moderne-andre-malraux.description: Inaugurated on 24 June 1961 by André Malraux, this glass-and-steel building, designed by Guy Lagneau and his team with Jean Prouvé, was the first museum built in France after the war. It holds more than two hundred works by Eugène Boudin, a collection of Raoul Dufy and Othon Friesz, and a rich Impressionist collection enriched by the Senn-Foulds donation.

mumig-musee-de-millau-et-des-grands-caus.name: MuMiG — Museum of Millau and the Grands Causses
mumig-musee-de-millau-et-des-grands-caus.description: Museum housed in the Hôtel de Pégayrolles, an 18th-century residence on place Foch in Millau. Its collections range from palaeontology and protohistory to the terra sigillata pottery of the Gallo-Roman workshop of La Graufesenque, and also tell the story of Millau's leather-dressing and glove-making trades and of the opera singer Emma Calvé.

mus-musee-d-histoire-urbaine-et-sociale-.name: MUS – Suresnes Museum of Urban and Social History
mus-musee-d-histoire-urbaine-et-sociale-.description: Museum of urban and social history housed in the former Suresnes-Longchamp railway station. It tells how the town was transformed in the 20th century, notably by Henri Sellier's garden city and the pioneering open-air school.

musee.name: Nogent-sur-Marne Intercommunal Museum
musee.description: Local history museum for the Marne riverbanks, telling how boating, bathing and riverside guinguettes made Nogent a centre of Parisian Sunday leisure from the 19th century. Paintings, posters and postcards document the surrounding communes.

musee-adrien-mentienne.name: Adrien Mentienne Museum
musee-adrien-mentienne.description: Bry-sur-Marne's municipal museum, named after a local historian and mayor. Alongside local history collections, it holds one of France's most important collections on Louis Daguerre, inventor of the daguerreotype, who spent his last years in Bry.

musee-alfred-bonno.name: Alfred Bonno Museum
musee-alfred-bonno.description: Chelles' archaeology museum, reopened in 2026 in fully redesigned spaces. Finds from local digs run from Palaeolithic flint tools to the Merovingian era, including rare early-medieval textiles linked to Queen Bathild and the royal abbey of Chelles.

musee-alsacien-de-haguenau.name: Alsatian Museum of Haguenau
musee-alsacien-de-haguenau.description: Museum of popular arts and traditions, housed since 1972 in the former chancellery of Haguenau, built around 1486 and in use until 1790. Across two floors, it brings together cast-iron fireback plates, popular imagery, reverse-glass paintings, Alsatian headdresses and costumes, pottery from Soufflenheim and Betschdorf, and a reconstructed peasant interior.

musee-anne-de-beaujeu.name: Anne-de-Beaujeu Museum
musee-anne-de-beaujeu.description: Departmental museum of the Allier, occupying the Renaissance pavilion of the former palace of the Dukes of Bourbon in Moulins. Opened in 1910 thanks to the bequest of the collector Louis Mantin, it holds a substantial archaeology section, late-medieval Bourbonnais sculpture, German and Flemish paintings, and Moulins faience.

musee-arcabas-en-chartreuse.name: Arcabas Museum in Chartreuse
musee-arcabas-en-chartreuse.description: The church of Saint-Hugues-de-Chartreuse, in the heart of the massif, entirely decorated by the painter Arcabas, who worked there from 1952 to 1992. Made a departmental museum of the Isère in 1984, the building brings together 111 works — canvases, stained glass, liturgical furnishings and a predella of 53 panels — among the most complete ensembles of 20th-century sacred art in France.

musee-archeologique-de-dijon.name: Dijon Archaeological Museum
musee-archeologique-de-dijon.description: Museum created in 1832 from the collections of Burgundian learned societies, housed since 1934 in the main wing of the former abbey of Saint-Bénigne, where it occupies the monks' Gothic dormitory and the Romanesque hall. It preserves the wooden votive offerings dedicated to the goddess Sequana at the source of the Seine, and a head of Christ by Claus Sluter.

musee-archeologique-de-saintes.name: Archaeological Museum of Saintes
musee-archeologique-de-saintes.description: Museum devoted to Mediolanum Santonum, capital of the Santones and one of the great cities of Roman Gaul. It houses one of the richest lapidary collections in France, made up of carved blocks from dismantled public monuments that were later reused in the late-antique rampart, complemented by objects of everyday Gallo-Roman life.

musee-archeologique-de-strasbourg.name: Strasbourg Archaeological Museum
musee-archeologique-de-strasbourg.description: Museum laid out in the vast basements of the Palais Rohan, whose collections trace back to the bequest of the scholar Jean-Daniel Schoepflin in the late 18th century. Reopened in 1992 after renovation, it unfolds across 1,200 square metres the history of Alsace from the Palaeolithic to the early Middle Ages, with a rich Gallo-Roman collection from Argentorate.

musee-archeologique-departemental-du-val.name: Val-d'Oise Archaeology Museum (MADVO)
musee-archeologique-departemental-du-val.description: The Val-d'Oise departmental archaeology museum, in the Vexin village of Guiry. Its chronological displays span prehistory to the 20th century, with finds from the Gallo-Roman site of Genainville and France's largest collection of Merovingian steles.

musee-archeologique-grenoble-saint-laure.name: Saint-Laurent Archaeological Museum, Grenoble
musee-archeologique-grenoble-saint-laure.description: Former church of Saint-Laurent, deconsecrated in 1983 after excavations uncovered more than 1,500 burials and nearly two millennia of funerary use. Reopened in 2011 beneath a glass-and-steel canopy, the site allows visitors to descend into the crypt of Saint-Oyand, a rare surviving example of early medieval architecture in Europe.

musee-arthur-rimbaud.name: Rimbaud Museum
musee-arthur-rimbaud.description: Set up in the Vieux Moulin, a mill built in 1626 on the Meuse whose façades have been listed since 1981, the museum opened in 1969. It preserves original manuscripts, including Voyelles, along with photographs, letters and objects brought back from Africa, largely from the collection donated in 1954 by Henri Matarasso.

musee-bargoin.name: Bargoin Museum
musee-bargoin.description: Museum born from the bequest made to Clermont-Ferrand in 1885 by the industrialist Jean-Baptiste Bargoin and inaugurated in 1903 in a building by the architect Joseph Dionnet. On the ground floor it presents regional archaeology, from prehistory to the Middle Ages, and upstairs a remarkable collection of textiles and carpets.

musee-bartholdi.name: Bartholdi Museum
musee-bartholdi.description: Birthplace of the sculptor Auguste Bartholdi, at 30 rue des Marchands in Colmar, converted into a museum in 1922. It preserves models, sketches, drawings and photographs relating to his great commissions, from the Statue of Liberty to the Lion of Belfort, and houses in its courtyard the bronze group Les Grands Soutiens du Monde.

musee-basque-et-de-l-histoire-de-bayonne.name: Basque Museum and History of Bayonne
musee-basque-et-de-l-histoire-de-bayonne.description: Ethnography museum housed in the Maison Dagourette, a residence from the late 16th century built on the quays of the Nive. Opened in 1924 and renovated in 2001, it presents, across some twenty rooms, everyday life in the Basque Country — herding, farming, games, dances — as well as the history of Bayonne.

musee-belmondo-et-de-la-sculpture-figura.name: Paul Belmondo Museum
musee-belmondo-et-de-la-sculpture-figura.description: Museum in the 18th-century Château Buchillot devoted to sculptor Paul Belmondo (1898-1982), a leading figure of 20th-century figurative sculpture. It shows his marbles, bronzes, medals and drawings, donated to Boulogne-Billancourt by his children.

musee-benoit-de-puydt.name: Benoît-De-Puydt Museum, Bailleul
musee-benoit-de-puydt.description: Museum born in 1859 from the bequest of Benoît De Puydt, a municipal tax collector and collector from Bailleul. Destroyed during the First World War and then rebuilt by the architect Maurice Dupire in the Flemish style, it preserves Flemish and Spanish paintings, Delft faience, Far Eastern porcelain, antique furniture and a room devoted to local folklore.

musee-bernard-d-agesci.name: Bernard-d'Agesci Museum
musee-bernard-d-agesci.description: Niort's multidisciplinary museum, opened in 2006 in the former girls' secondary school built in 1897 by the architect Georges Lasseron. It bears the name of the Niort painter Bernard d'Agesci, founder of the town's first public library and drawing school, and brings together fine arts from the 16th to the 19th century, natural history, and a collection on the history of education.

musee-bibliotheque-pierre-andre-benoit-p.name: Pierre-André-Benoit Museum-Library (PAB)
musee-bibliotheque-pierre-andre-benoit-p.description: Museum set up in the Château de Rochebelle, a residence of medieval origin remodelled in the neoclassical style in the late 18th century by the mining concessionaire François-Pierre de Tubeuf. Opened in 1989 following the donation made to Alès by the printer and poet Pierre-André Benoit, it preserves his artists' books and works by Picasso, Braque, Miró and Picabia.

musee-blanche-hoschede-monet-ancien-muse.name: Blanche Hoschedé-Monet Museum (former A.G. Poulain Museum)
musee-blanche-hoschede-monet-ancien-muse.description: Vernon's museum, founded in 1862 around a collection of taxidermy birds, housed since 1983 in the Lemoine de Belle-Isle mansion and renamed in 2024 after Claude Monet's stepdaughter. It brings together Impressionist paintings from the Giverny artists' colony and a substantial collection of animal art by Pompon, Bugatti and Jouve.

musee-bonnat-helleu-musee-des-beaux-arts.name: Bonnat-Helleu Museum
musee-bonnat-helleu-musee-des-beaux-arts.description: Bayonne's museum of fine arts, born from the donation made in 1891 by the painter Léon Bonnat and housed in a building by Charles Planckaert inaugurated in 1901. Renamed in 2011 after the addition of the Paul-César Helleu collection, it preserves paintings by El Greco, Rubens, Goya and Degas, and one of the finest collections of drawings in France.

musee-bossuet.name: Bossuet Museum
musee-bossuet.description: Meaux's fine-arts museum in the former episcopal palace beside the cathedral, named after Bossuet, the city's celebrated 17th-century bishop and preacher. It shows paintings and sculpture from the 16th to 19th centuries, with a mitre-shaped garden attributed to Le Nôtre.

musee-bourdelle.name: Bourdelle Museum
musee-bourdelle.description: The Montparnasse studios and gardens where sculptor Antoine Bourdelle, a pupil and assistant of Rodin, lived and worked. Plasters, marbles and monumental bronzes such as Hercules the Archer are shown in the preserved workshops and a modern extension.

musee-calvet.name: Calvet Museum
musee-calvet.description: Museum born from the bequest made in 1810 by the Avignon physician and collector Esprit Calvet, authorised by imperial decree the following year. Since 1833 it has occupied the Hôtel de Villeneuve-Martignan, built in the 18th century to designs by Jean-Baptiste Franque, and displays archaeology, 15th- to 20th-century painting, sculpture and decorative arts.

musee-camille-claudel.name: Camille Claudel Museum
musee-camille-claudel.description: Opened in 2017 in Nogent-sur-Seine, where Camille Claudel spent her adolescence, it continues the museum created in 1902 by the sculptors Alfred Boucher and Paul Dubois. Designed by the architect Adelfo Scaranello around the 18th-century family house, it holds the largest public collection of the artist's work.

musee-cantini.name: Cantini Museum
musee-cantini.description: Housed in the Hôtel de Montgrand, a mansion built in 1694, acquired and then bequeathed to the city by the sculptor Jules Cantini in 1916. Opened in 1936, it holds one of the leading French collections of modern art from 1900 to 1980, rich in Surrealist paintings linked to the movement's stay in Marseille in 1940-1941.

musee-carnavalet-histoire-de-paris.name: Carnavalet Museum
musee-carnavalet-histoire-de-paris.description: The museum of the history of Paris, set in two Marais mansions including the Hôtel Carnavalet, once home to the letter-writer Madame de Sévigné. Its collections run from prehistoric canoes to the French Revolution and the modern city.

musee-cernuschi-musee-des-arts-de-l-asie.name: Cernuschi Museum
musee-cernuschi-musee-des-arts-de-l-asie.description: The City of Paris's Asian art museum, built around the collection of banker Henri Cernuschi in his mansion beside Parc Monceau. It is noted for its ancient Chinese bronzes and a monumental Japanese Buddha brought from Meguro.

musee-champollion.name: Champollion Museum
musee-champollion.description: Departmental museum of the Isère, set up in the Domaine des Ombrages, an 18th-century manor house that was the family property of the Champollion brothers. Reopened in 2021 after restoration, it traces the life of Jean-François Champollion, decipherer of the hieroglyphs, and his brother Jacques-Joseph through some 1,400 objects, including Egyptian antiquities on loan from the Louvre.

musee-chateau-d-annecy.name: Château-Musée d'Annecy
musee-chateau-d-annecy.description: Former residence of the Counts of Geneva and later the Dukes of Nemours, overlooking the old town, the château was bought by the municipality in 1952 and has housed the municipal collections since 1956. Alpine archaeology, regional art, contemporary art and natural science sit side by side, with more than 10,000 ethnographic objects.

musee-chateau-de-villeveque.name: Château de Villevêque
musee-chateau-de-villeveque.description: Former residence of the bishops of Angers, first mentioned in 1025 and rebuilt between 1448 and 1465 by Jean de Beauvau after the Hundred Years' War. Bequeathed to the city of Angers in 2003 by the collector Daniel Duclaux, it displays more than nine hundred works: medieval sculpture, tapestries, ceramics and manuscripts.

musee-christian-dior.name: Christian Dior Museum
musee-christian-dior.description: Housed in the Villa Les Rhumbs, a Belle Époque residence overlooking the sea where the couturier Christian Dior spent his childhood, set within the garden designed by his mother. Now owned by the town, it houses the only Musée de France-labelled museum devoted to a fashion designer, with some three hundred wardrobe pieces.

musee-cognacq-jay-musee-du-xviiie-siecle.name: Cognacq-Jay Museum
musee-cognacq-jay-musee-du-xviiie-siecle.description: An intimate museum of 18th-century art in the Hôtel Donon in the Marais, formed from the collection of Ernest Cognacq, founder of La Samaritaine department store: paintings by Boucher, Fragonard and Chardin, pastels, porcelain and furniture.

musee-crozatier.name: Crozatier Museum
musee-crozatier.description: Museum of Le Puy-en-Velay, set within the Jardin Henri-Vinay, inaugurated in 1868 thanks to the bequest of the bronze founder Charles Crozatier, whose name it bears. Reopened in 2018 after lengthy renovation, it spans fine arts, archaeology, natural science and technology, along with a collection devoted to Le Puy lace.

musee-curie.name: Curie Museum
musee-curie.description: Housed in Marie Curie's former laboratory at the Radium Institute, where she worked until her death in 1934, the museum preserves her office and chemistry lab and traces the history of radioactivity and a family awarded five Nobel Prizes.

musee-d-angouleme.name: Angoulême Museum
musee-d-angouleme.description: Housed since 1920 in the former bishop's palace, at the foot of the cathedral, and entirely renovated between 2002 and 2008. It presents the archaeology and palaeontology of the Charente region, including the Agris helmet, a gold-plated iron Celtic helmet from the 4th century BCE, a substantial collection of African and Oceanic art, and European paintings.

musee-d-aquitaine.name: Museum of Aquitaine
musee-d-aquitaine.description: Created in 1962, this museum of history and civilisations has occupied since 1987 the former Faculty of Arts and Sciences, built in the 1880s. It traces the past of Bordeaux and Aquitaine, from the Venus with the Horn of Laussel to the permanent galleries devoted to colonial trade and the slave trade.

musee-d-archeologie-bastion-saint-andre.name: Bastion Saint-André
musee-d-archeologie-bastion-saint-andre.description: A bastion in the fortifications of Antibes, built in the late 17th century following Vauban's inspections and completed around 1710. Since 1963 it has housed the city's archaeology museum, grown from the collection assembled from 1928 by Romuald Dor de la Souchère and devoted to the Greek and Roman past of Antipolis.

musee-d-archeologie-de-nice-cimiez.name: Nice-Cimiez Archaeology Museum
musee-d-archeologie-de-nice-cimiez.description: A museum built on the ancient site of Cemenelum, Roman capital of the Alpes-Maritimes, on the hill of Cimiez. Founded in 1960 and housed since 1989 in a building by Wladimir Mitrofanoff overlooking the remains of the baths and the early Christian baptistery, it displays ceramics, milestones, sculptures and funerary objects from antiquity.

musee-d-archeologie-mediterraneenne-mam.name: Museum of Mediterranean Archaeology
musee-d-archeologie-mediterraneenne-mam.description: Housed on the first floor of the Vieille Charité, a former Marseille almshouse built in the 17th and 18th centuries to plans by Pierre Puget. It holds France's second-largest Egyptian collection, drawn mainly from the cabinet of Doctor Clot-Bey, alongside a survey devoted to Mesopotamia, Cyprus, Greece, Etruria and Rome.

musee-d-archeologie-nationale-des-origin.name: National Archaeology Museum
musee-d-archeologie-nationale-des-origin.description: France's national archaeology museum occupies the royal château of Saint-Germain-en-Laye, rebuilt under François I. Its collections run from the Palaeolithic to the early Middle Ages and include the 25,000-year-old Lady of Brassempouy.

musee-d-art-contemporain-du-val-de-marne.name: Val-de-Marne Museum of Contemporary Art (MAC VAL)
musee-d-art-contemporain-du-val-de-marne.description: Opened in 2005 in Vitry-sur-Seine, MAC VAL was the first museum devoted solely to contemporary art made in France since the 1950s. Its collection is shown in regularly renewed displays, alongside temporary exhibitions and a sculpture garden.

musee-d-art-contemporain-mac.name: Lyon Museum of Contemporary Art
musee-d-art-contemporain-mac.description: Founded in 1984 in a wing of the Fine Arts Museum, the macLYON moved in 1995 to the Cité Internationale, into a building by Renzo Piano that preserves the façade of the former Palais de la Foire. Its fully modular spaces host the city's contemporary collection and the Lyon Biennale of Contemporary Art.

musee-d-art-de-toulon-mat.name: Toulon Art Museum
musee-d-art-de-toulon-mat.description: A Neo-Renaissance building erected between 1883 and 1888 by the Toulon architect Gaudensi Allar and opened as a municipal museum-library. Renovated and enlarged between 2018 and 2021, it shows paintings from the 15th to the 20th century, contemporary art since the 1960s, and a substantial photography collection.

musee-d-art-et-d-archeologie-d-aurillac.name: Aurillac Museum of Art and Archaeology
musee-d-art-et-d-archeologie-d-aurillac.description: A Cantal museum set in a former 17th-century Visitandine convent, later a national stud farm in the 19th century, then converted into a museum in 1992 within the Pierre-Mendès-France cultural centre. Its collections span archaeology from the Palaeolithic to the Gallo-Roman period, the traditions of Haute-Auvergne, and paintings and sculptures from the 17th to 19th centuries.

musee-d-art-et-d-archeologie-de-senlis.name: Senlis Museum of Art and Archaeology
musee-d-art-et-d-archeologie-de-senlis.description: Founded in 1867 by the archaeological committee and returned in 1989 to the former episcopal palace, a building combining Gallo-Roman foundations, a 13th-century chapel and a Renaissance gallery. It holds antique remains, nearly three hundred votive offerings from the Gallo-Roman temple in the forest of Halatte, and paintings by Thomas Couture.

musee-d-art-et-d-archeologie-du-pays-de-.name: Laon Museum of Art and Archaeology
musee-d-art-et-d-archeologie-du-pays-de-.description: Founded in 1861 and housed since 1891 in a former Templar commandery whose octagonal chapel dates from the 12th century. It brings together European paintings from the 15th to the 19th century, regional archaeology, and a collection of nearly 1,700 Mediterranean antiquities, one of the largest in France after the Louvre's.

musee-d-art-et-d-archeologie-du-perigord.name: Périgord Museum of Art and Archaeology
musee-d-art-et-d-archeologie-du-perigord.description: Successor to the museum founded in 1804 by Wlgrin de Taillefer, it occupies the former Augustinian convent of Périgueux, rebuilt from 1895 to 1898 by the architect Charles Planckaert and opened in 1903. Its collections include one of France's richest prehistoric holdings, Gallo-Roman mosaics from Vesunna, and African and Oceanic art.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire.name: Meudon Museum of Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire.description: Meudon's museum of art and history occupies the town's oldest house, once home to royal surgeon Ambroise Paré and later to Molière's widow Armande Béjart. It covers local history and landscape painting, with 20th-century sculpture in the garden.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-antoine-vivene.name: Antoine Vivenel Museum of Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-antoine-vivene.description: A museum born from the gift made to Compiègne in 1839 by the entrepreneur and patron Antoine Vivenel (1799–1862), who dreamed of an encyclopaedic collection spanning every art and every age. Housed since 1952 in the Hôtel de Songeons-Bicquilley, it presents Gaulish and Gallo-Roman archaeology, Greek vases, Italian faience and French paintings.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-chaumont.name: Chaumont Museum of Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-chaumont.description: Opened in 1965, the Chaumont museum occupies seven rooms of the 13th- and 14th-century palace of the counts of Champagne, along with the nineteen-metre keep that served as a prison until 1886. It brings together regional archaeology, medieval sculpture, paintings, and a collection devoted to the glove-making industry of Haute-Marne.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-de-cholet.name: Cholet Museum of Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-de-cholet.description: A museum opened in 1993, formed from the merger of the history and art sections created by the city in the late 1970s. Its art gallery brings together 18th- and 19th-century paintings and abstract works by François Morellet and Vasarely; its history gallery is devoted to the Wars of the Vendée.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-de-l-hopital-s.name: Sainte-Anne Hospital Museum of Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-de-l-hopital-s.description: A museum inside the Sainte-Anne psychiatric hospital in the 14th arrondissement, presenting the hospital's collection of works made by patients, assembled since the mid-20th century — a major ensemble of art brut — alongside temporary exhibitions.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-de-lisieux.name: Lisieux Museum of Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-de-lisieux.description: A museum set in one of the last surviving 17th-century timber-framed houses in Lisieux, listed as a historic monument in 1959. Reopened in 2013, it traces the city's history from the Palaeolithic to the post-war reconstruction and holds the most complete public collection of Pré-d'Auge ceramics.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-de-provence-ma.name: Museum of Art and History of Provence
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-de-provence-ma.description: A museum set in the Hôtel de Clapiers-Cabris, a mansion built from 1772 to 1774 for the Marquis de Cabris, Mirabeau's brother-in-law. Founded in 1921 as the Musée Fragonard on the initiative of François Carnot, it presents the history and arts of eastern Provence, with a rich collection of regional faience.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-de-saint-brieu.name: Saint-Brieuc Museum of Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-de-saint-brieu.description: A museum of art, history and ethnography for the Côtes-d'Armor, housed since the mid-1980s in a former gendarmerie barracks in Saint-Brieuc. Its collections evoke fishing and maritime life, textiles, Breton costume and regional arts, with works by Alfred Guillou and Mathurin Méheut.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-de-saint-lo.name: Saint-Lô Museum of Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-de-saint-lo.description: A museum whose collections date back to 1835; after its building was destroyed in 1944, it has occupied the Jean-Lurçat cultural centre, designed by the architect Eugène Leseney, since 1989. It holds the Amours de Gombaut et Macée tapestry, woven in Bruges in the 16th century, tapestries by Lurçat, and paintings by Corot, Boudin and Léger.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-du-judaisme.name: Museum of Jewish Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-du-judaisme.description: Housed in the 17th-century Hôtel de Saint-Aignan in the Marais, the museum traces Jewish art and history from the Middle Ages to today, with ceremonial objects, archives of the Dreyfus affair and works by Chagall, Modigliani and Soutine.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-guy-baillet.name: Guy Baillet Museum of Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-guy-baillet.description: Langres' museum of art and history, set in a contemporary building opened in 1997 that incorporates the Romanesque chapel of Saint-Didier. Enriched since the 19th century by collectors' gifts, its collections range from Gallo-Roman archaeology — including the Bacchus mosaic and Celtic torcs — to old master paintings, among them a Ribera.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-hotel-beurnier.name: Museum of Art and History – Hôtel Beurnier-Rossel
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-hotel-beurnier.description: A mansion built from 1774 for Georges-David Rossel and Anne-Madeleine Beurnier to designs by the architect Philippe de La Guépière, bequeathed to the city in 1917. It evokes the principality of Montbéliard in the 18th and 19th centuries, with Couleru marquetry furniture, Protestant devotional objects and musical boxes from Sainte-Suzanne.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-louis-senlecq.name: Louis Senlecq Museum of Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-louis-senlecq.description: L'Isle-Adam's museum of art and history, in an 18th-century mansion, holds one of the finest collections of the landscape painter Jules Dupré, a Barbizon-school figure who kept his studio in the town, alongside works on local heritage.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-marcel-dessal.name: Dreux Museum of Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-marcel-dessal.description: Set in a Neo-Romanesque chapel built in 1895 for the Saint-Pierre boarding school and bought by the city in 1908. Opened in 1950 and renamed the Musée Marcel-Dessal in 1977, it brings together archaeology, decorative arts, sculptures from the former collegiate church of Saint-Étienne, and paintings from the 16th to the 20th century.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-michel-hachet.name: Michel Hachet Museum of Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-michel-hachet.description: Toul's municipal museum, in Meurthe-et-Moselle, on rue Gouvion-Saint-Cyr at the heart of the former episcopal city. Named after Michel Hachet, it presents archaeology, art and history collections devoted to Toul and the Toulois, as well as temporary exhibitions.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-paul-eluard.name: Paul Éluard Museum of Art and History
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-paul-eluard.description: Saint-Denis's museum of art and history is set in a former Carmelite convent where Louis XV's daughter Louise was a nun. Collections range from the convent's restored cells to the Paris Commune of 1871 and the poet Paul Éluard, born in the town.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-saint-germain-.name: Saint-Germain Museum
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-saint-germain-.description: A former Benedictine abbey built over the tomb of Saint Germain, bishop of Auxerre in the 5th century, whose Carolingian crypts preserve 9th-century frescoes among the oldest in France. The monastic buildings house an archaeology museum spanning prehistory to the Middle Ages.

musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-saint-leger-an.name: Saint-Léger Museum of Art and History (former Saint-Léger Abbey)
musee-d-art-et-d-histoire-saint-leger-an.description: A museum set in the former Saint-Léger Abbey, founded in 1139 for canons regular, turned into a brewery at the end of the 18th century and then a junior seminary in the 19th. Becoming the municipal museum in the early 20th century, it holds Soissons' archaeology, history and fine art collections.

musee-d-art-et-d-industrie-de-saint-etie.name: Saint-Étienne Museum of Art and Industry
musee-d-art-et-d-industrie-de-saint-etie.description: Founded in 1889 in the former Palais des Arts, a building erected from 1846 to 1851 by the architect Étienne Boisson. It traces the three trades that made Saint-Étienne's name: ribbon-weaving, with the world's largest collection and its Jacquard looms; firearms, France's second-largest collection; and the bicycle.

musee-d-art-hyacinthe-rigaud.name: Hyacinthe Rigaud Museum
musee-d-art-hyacinthe-rigaud.description: Founded in 1820 and renamed in 1959 after the Perpignan-born portraitist Hyacinthe Rigaud, the museum has united the Hôtel de Lazerme and the Hôtel de Mailly since 2017. It presents Catalan Gothic art, portraits by Rigaud, and modern works by Picasso, Maillol and Dufy.

musee-d-art-moderne-collections-national.name: Museum of Modern Art – Pierre and Denise Lévy National Collections
musee-d-art-moderne-collections-national.description: A museum born of the gift made to the State by the Troyes industrialists Pierre and Denise Lévy, set in the former episcopal palace near the cathedral. Reopened in 2024 after renovation, it brings together paintings and sculptures from Courbet to Nicolas de Staël, with a major group of works by André Derain and the glassware of Maurice Marinot.

musee-d-art-moderne-de-la-ville-de-paris.name: Paris Museum of Modern Art
musee-d-art-moderne-de-la-ville-de-paris.description: The City of Paris's modern art museum, in the east wing of the 1937 Palais de Tokyo, spans 20th- and 21st-century art from Fauvism to today, with major works by Matisse, Delaunay and Dufy, including his vast mural 'La Fée Électricité'.

musee-d-art-moderne-donation-maurice-jar.name: Belfort Museum of Modern Art
musee-d-art-moderne-donation-maurice-jar.description: A museum opened in 1999 in the former house of the Belfort-born poet Léon Deubel, fitted out by the architects Robert Rebutato and Pernette Perriand to recreate the atmosphere of a gallery. It presents the 112 works given to the city in 1997 by Maurice Jardot, director of the Galerie Louise Leiris, including works by Picasso, Braque, Léger and Chagall.

musee-d-art-moderne-et-contemporain-de-s.name: Strasbourg Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art
musee-d-art-moderne-et-contemporain-de-s.description: Opened in December 1998, it occupies a glass building designed by the architect Adrien Fainsilber, on the banks of the Ill facing Petite France. The only major French museum to cover an unbroken span from 1870 to the present day, it holds groups of works by Arp, Kandinsky and Brauner, and Gustave Doré's Christ Leaving the Praetorium.

musee-d-art-moderne-et-d-art-contemporai.name: Nice Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art
musee-d-art-moderne-et-d-art-contemporai.description: Opened in June 1990, it occupies a white Carrara marble building shaped as a four-towered arch spanning the Paillon, designed by the architects Yves Bayard and Henri Vidal. Its collections trace art since the late 1950s: Nouveau Réalisme from Nice with Klein, Arman and Raysse, American Pop Art, and the Niki de Saint Phalle donation.

musee-d-art-moderne-richard-anacreon-mam.name: Richard Anacréon Museum of Modern Art
musee-d-art-moderne-richard-anacreon-mam.description: A museum formed from the collection bequeathed to Granville by the bookseller and bibliophile Richard Anacréon (1907–1992), set in the former Paul-Bert school in the upper town. It brings together paintings and graphic works by Derain, Dufy, Signac, Vlaminck and Pascin, sculptures by Rodin and Bourdelle, and rare inscribed editions.

musee-d-art-sacre.name: Dijon Museum of Sacred Art
musee-d-art-sacre.description: A museum set in the church of Sainte-Anne, a former chapel of the Bernardine monastery acquired by the city in 1950 and opened as a museum in 1980. It presents Burgundian Catholic sacred art from the 12th to the 19th century: sculpture, goldsmith's work, reliquaries, liturgical ornaments, and the black marble baldachin carved by Jean Dubois in 1675.

musee-d-arts-africains-oceaniens-amerind.name: Museum of African, Oceanic and American Indian Arts
musee-d-arts-africains-oceaniens-amerind.description: Opened in 1992 on the second floor of the Vieille Charité, a 17th-century Baroque ensemble built by Pierre Puget, this museum presents the arts of Africa, Oceania and the Americas. On display are African masks and statues from the Pierre Guerre donation, Oceanic overmodelled skulls, and Mexican folk art.

musee-d-arts-de-nantes.name: Nantes Arts Museum
musee-d-arts-de-nantes.description: A Palais des Arts opened in 1900, designed by the Nantes architect Clément Josso and arranged around a patio topped by a glass roof. Enlarged by the firm Stanton Williams and reopened in 2017 with the translucent marble Cube, it displays more than nine hundred works from the 13th century to the present, from the Italian primitives of the Cacault collection to contemporary art.

musee-d-ennery.name: D'Ennery Museum
musee-d-ennery.description: A house-museum on avenue Foch attached to the Musée Guimet, preserving the Japanese and Chinese art collected by Clémence d'Ennery in the 19th century — netsuke, ceramics and fantastic creatures — in its original Second Empire interiors.

musee-d-ethnographie-de-bordeaux-meb.name: University of Bordeaux Museum of Ethnography
musee-d-ethnographie-de-bordeaux-meb.description: Founded in 1894 by Albert Pitres, dean of the medical faculty, this university museum occupies the former premises of the faculty of medicine and pharmacy on place de la Victoire, built by Jean-Louis Pascal. Forgotten after 1918 and reopened to the public in 2011, it holds some six thousand objects from all five continents.

musee-d-evreux-ancien-eveche-musee-d-art.name: Évreux Museum of Art, History and Archaeology
musee-d-evreux-ancien-eveche-musee-d-art.description: A museum founded in 1873 and moved in 1961 into the former bishop's palace dating from the late 15th century, backed onto the Gallo-Roman wall and linked to Notre-Dame cathedral by a cloister. It presents the archaeology of the city and of the sanctuary of Gisacum, including a bronze Jupiter, Aubusson tapestries, and paintings from the 17th to the 20th century.

musee-d-histoire-de-belfort-citadelle.name: Belfort History Museum (Citadel)
musee-d-histoire-de-belfort-citadelle.description: A museum set at the heart of the Citadel of Belfort, a stronghold remodelled first by Vauban and then by Haxo. It traces the settlement of the land between the Vosges and the Jura from prehistory to the Middle Ages, the growth of the town, and the siege of 1870–71 led by Colonel Denfert-Rochereau, and devotes six rooms to the sculptor Frédéric-Auguste Bartholdi.

musee-d-histoire-de-marseille-mhm.name: Marseille History Museum (MHM)
musee-d-histoire-de-marseille-mhm.description: Founded in 1983 following the archaeological discoveries made during construction of the Centre Bourse, it is the largest urban history museum in France. Entirely renovated by the architect Roland Carta and reopened in 2013, it unfolds twenty-six centuries of Marseille's history across thirteen sequences and adjoins the ancient Greek harbour, now the Jardin des Vestiges.

musee-d-histoire-locale-memoire-de-la-vi.name: Rueil-Malmaison Museum of Local History
musee-d-histoire-locale-memoire-de-la-vi.description: A local history museum in Rueil-Malmaison's former 19th-century town hall, covering the town from its origins to today, with figurine displays of Napoleon's Grande Armée and mementoes of Empress Joséphine, who lived at nearby Malmaison.

musee-d-initiation-a-la-nature-cpie.name: Museum of Nature Discovery
musee-d-initiation-a-la-nature-cpie.description: Set in a former bakery of the Abbaye aux Hommes, this small museum, created in 1974, bills itself as the smallest natural history museum in France. It introduces visitors to Norman wildlife, taxidermied birds foremost among them, as well as a garden of regional wild plants.

musee-d-orsay.name: Musée d'Orsay
musee-d-orsay.description: Set in the former Orsay railway station, built for the 1900 World's Fair, the museum holds the world's richest collection of Impressionist and Post-Impressionist painting — Monet, Renoir, Degas, Van Gogh — and French art from 1848 to 1914.

musee-daubigny.name: Daubigny Museum
musee-daubigny.description: A museum in the 17th-century Manoir des Colombières in Auvers-sur-Oise devoted to Charles-François Daubigny, a forerunner of Impressionism, with works by his circle and the painters of the Oise valley, plus collections of naïve and feline-themed art.

musee-dauphinois.name: Dauphinois Museum
musee-dauphinois.description: Founded in 1906 by Hippolyte Müller, it was one of the very first regional heritage museums in France. It occupies the former 17th-century Visitandine convent of Sainte-Marie-d'en-Haut, clinging to the lower slopes of the Bastille, and devotes its exhibitions to the history and Alpine cultures of the Dauphiné.

musee-de-bourgoin-jallieu.name: Bourgoin-Jallieu Museum
musee-de-bourgoin-jallieu.description: Founded in 1929 on the initiative of the painter Victor Charreton and opened in 1933, it occupies the former Antonin chapel, built in 1503, adjoining an 18th-century hospital. Its collections trace the history of fabric printing, a local speciality, and present canvases by Charreton and Bellet du Poisat.

musee-de-bretagne-les-champs-libres.name: Les Champs Libres
musee-de-bretagne-les-champs-libres.description: A museum of society devoted to the history and cultures of Brittany, from prehistory to the present day. It has been housed since March 2006 at Les Champs Libres, a large Rennes complex designed by Christian de Portzamparc that also brings together the Rennes Métropole library and the Espace des Sciences.

musee-de-cambrai-musee-des-beaux-arts.name: Cambrai Museum
musee-de-cambrai-musee-des-beaux-arts.description: Founded in 1847 from works seized during the Revolution, the museum moved in 1893 into the Hôtel de Francqueville, an 18th-century mansion enlarged between 1989 and 1994. It brings together archaeological collections, a fine art gallery featuring Rodin, Camille Claudel and Matisse, and nearly 1,500 works of geometric abstraction.

musee-de-flandre.name: Flanders Museum
musee-de-flandre.description: Set in the Hôtel de la Noble Cour, seat of Cassel's former feudal court, built in the 16th century and listed as a historic monument in 1910, this museum reopened in October 2010 after thirteen years of restoration. Its some 6,000 works explore Flemish art, from Jan Gossaert and Quentin Metsys to prints after Bruegel.

musee-de-grenoble.name: Grenoble Museum
musee-de-grenoble.description: Founded on 16 February 1798 by the drawing teacher Louis-Joseph Jay, it became, thanks to one of its curators between the wars, the first museum of modern art in France. Housed since 1994 on place de Lavalette, it spreads across fifty-seven rooms collections ranging from ancient Egypt to contemporary art, including Matisse's Interior with Aubergines.

musee-de-l-air-et-de-l-espace.name: Air and Space Museum
musee-de-l-air-et-de-l-espace.description: One of the world's oldest aviation museums, founded in 1919 at Paris–Le Bourget airport. Its collection runs from pioneer-era flying machines to Concorde airliners and Ariane rockets, displayed in the 1937 terminal building and on the tarmac.

musee-de-l-ancien-eveche.name: Museum of the Former Bishop's Palace
musee-de-l-ancien-eveche.description: A departmental museum set in the former palace of the bishops of Grenoble, opened in 1998 at the end of an extensive heritage restoration around place Notre-Dame. Its archaeological basement preserves the city's early Christian baptistery, uncovered during excavations, while the exhibition traces the history and heritage of the Isère.

musee-de-l-ardenne.name: Ardennes Museum
musee-de-l-ardenne.description: Opened on 20 October 1994 in 17th- to 20th-century buildings on the place Ducale, complemented by a glass-and-steel extension, it unfolds a chronological tour across 3,400 square metres. Visitors discover Celtic chariot burials, weapons from the Charleville manufactory, an apothecary's shop of 1756, and two puppet galleries.

musee-de-l-armee.name: Army Museum
musee-de-l-armee.description: France's military history museum at Les Invalides, the veterans' complex built by Louis XIV. Its collections span medieval armour to the two World Wars, and the golden-domed church shelters the tomb of Napoleon I.

musee-de-l-echevinage.name: Échevinage Museum of Saintes
musee-de-l-echevinage.description: Set in the former échevinage (aldermen's hall) of Saintes, whose octagonal belfry dates from the 15th century and main building from the 18th, the museum was born of Count Lemercier's bequest in 1864 and has occupied these premises since 1978. It presents 19th-century paintings, the Saintonge and Bordeaux schools, and Sèvres porcelain.

musee-de-l-ecole-de-barbizon-auberge-gan.name: Museum of the Barbizon School – Auberge Ganne
musee-de-l-ecole-de-barbizon-auberge-gan.description: The former Ganne inn in Barbizon, where landscape painters lodged from the 1820s, keeps walls and cupboards covered with their painted decorations. The museum recounts the school led by Millet and Théodore Rousseau at the edge of Fontainebleau forest.

musee-de-l-ecole-de-nancy.name: Museum of the École de Nancy
musee-de-l-ecole-de-nancy.description: Set in the former estate of Eugène Corbin, a leading patron of the movement, this museum, opened in its present form in 1964, is devoted to the Art Nouveau of Nancy. It presents reconstructed period interiors and creations by Émile Gallé, Louis Majorelle, Victor Prouvé, Jacques Gruber and the Daum manufactory.

musee-de-l-ecole-nationale-superieure-de.name: Museum of the École Nationale Supérieure des Beaux-Arts
musee-de-l-ecole-nationale-superieure-de.description: The collection of France's historic fine-arts school holds some 450,000 works, from old-master drawings and prints to Prix de Rome student pieces, shown in temporary exhibitions in the school's buildings on the Left Bank.

musee-de-l-histoire-vivante.name: Museum of Living History
musee-de-l-histoire-vivante.description: A museum of French social and working-class history, founded in 1937 and set in a mansion in Montreuil's Parc Montreau. Photographs, prints and objects trace the labour movement and political struggles from the Revolution to today.

musee-de-l-hospice-comtesse.name: Hospice Comtesse Museum
musee-de-l-hospice-comtesse.description: A former hospital founded in 1237 by Jeanne de Constantinople, Countess of Flanders, at the heart of Vieux-Lille, it has housed the city's museum of art and history since 1962. Displayed in the buildings of the Augustinian community that ran the hospital until 1793, its collections evoke Lille's past and Flemish decorative arts.

musee-de-l-hotel-dieu.name: Museum of the Hôtel-Dieu
musee-de-l-hotel-dieu.description: Mantes-la-Jolie's fine-arts museum occupies the listed former chapel of the town's Hôtel-Dieu hospital, renovated in 2018. It holds France's most important public collection of works by the Neo-Impressionist painter Maximilien Luce.

musee-de-l-hotel-sandelin.name: Hôtel Sandelin Museum
musee-de-l-hotel-sandelin.description: A Louis XV-style mansion built in 1776–77 for Marie-Josèphe Sandelin, acquired by the city of Saint-Omer in 1899 to house a museum that opened in 1904. It holds French and Flemish paintings from the 16th to 18th centuries, some 4,000 ceramics from Saint-Omer, Rouen and Delft, and a substantial coin collection.

musee-de-l-illustration-jeunesse-mij.name: Museum of Children's Book Illustration
musee-de-l-illustration-jeunesse-mij.description: Opened in 2005 in the Hôtel de Mora, a Moulins mansion built in 1750 and protected as a historic monument, it is devoted to the illustration of children's books. Its collections bring together more than 3,800 original drawings, from Gustave Doré and Rodolphe Töpffer to Kitty Crowther and Beatrice Alemagna.

musee-de-l-image-imagerie-d-epinal.name: Imagerie d'Épinal
musee-de-l-image-imagerie-d-epinal.description: A museum devoted to popular printed imagery, opened in 2003 opposite the Imagerie d'Épinal, a manufactory founded in 1796 by Jean-Charles Pellerin that spread the famous images d'Épinal throughout France. Its collection brings together more than 110,000 French and foreign prints, from the 16th century to the present day.

musee-de-l-industrie-textile.name: Museum of the Textile Industry
musee-de-l-industrie-textile.description: Set in the Gère valley, Vienne's industrial cradle, in a factory building erected in 1919 to designs by the architect Henri Poussin, it opened to the public on 21 September 2019. Machines, archives and objects trace the manufacture of textiles and working-class life in the 19th and 20th centuries.

musee-de-l-institut-du-monde-arabe.name: Arab World Institute Museum
musee-de-l-institut-du-monde-arabe.description: The Arab World Institute's museum surveys the arts and civilisations of the Arab world, from pre-Islamic antiquity to contemporary creation, inside Jean Nouvel's landmark 1987 building with its light-filtering geometric facade.

musee-de-l-orangerie-des-tuileries.name: Musée de l'Orangerie
musee-de-l-orangerie-des-tuileries.description: A former Tuileries orangery now displaying Monet's monumental Water Lilies cycle in two oval rooms designed for it, alongside the Walter-Guillaume collection of Renoir, Cézanne, Matisse, Picasso and Modigliani.

musee-de-l-uvre-notre-dame.name: Musée de l'Œuvre Notre-Dame
musee-de-l-uvre-notre-dame.description: Set in the buildings of the Fondation de l'Œuvre Notre-Dame, responsible since the Middle Ages for building and maintaining the cathedral, it presents the arts of the Upper Rhine up to Strasbourg's annexation by France in 1681. On display are the cathedral's original statues, its stained glass, and Gothic architectural drawings.

musee-de-la-bataille-de-fromelles.name: Museum of the Battle of Fromelles
musee-de-la-bataille-de-fromelles.description: A museum devoted to the First World War, set in Fromelles near the Pheasant Wood military cemetery. It pays tribute to the Australian and British soldiers who fell in the battle of 19–20 July 1916 and recounts the exhumation and subsequent identification of the bodies found in the wood's pits.

musee-de-la-batellerie.name: Museum of Inland Waterways
musee-de-la-batellerie.description: Set in the Château du Prieuré overlooking Conflans-Sainte-Honorine, the historic capital of France's barge people, this museum traces inland waterway navigation through ship models, tools and documents on canals, towing and river trade.

musee-de-la-ceramique.name: Rouen Ceramics Museum
musee-de-la-ceramique.description: Founded in 1864, the museum has occupied the Hôtel d'Hocqueville since 1984, a 17th-century mansion built on the remains of the old château of Rouen. Its some 6,000 pieces make it one of the great repositories of Rouen faience, complemented by French and foreign production.

musee-de-la-chartreuse-de-douai.name: Chartreuse Museum of Douai
musee-de-la-chartreuse-de-douai.description: The museum occupies a Renaissance mansion built in 1559 by Jacques d'Abancourt, enlarged in 1608 and then acquired in 1662 by Carthusian monks, who added a chapel, refectory and chapter house. Opened in 1958, it brings together more than 10,000 works, including Jean Bellegambe's Anchin polyptych and Flemish and Italian paintings.

musee-de-la-chasse-et-de-la-nature.name: Museum of Hunting and Nature
musee-de-la-chasse-et-de-la-nature.description: In two Marais mansions, the Hôtel de Guénégaud and Hôtel de Mongelas, this museum explores the relationship between humans and animals, mixing old-master paintings, taxidermy, historic weapons and contemporary art.

musee-de-la-corse-museu-di-a-corsica.name: Museum of Corsica / Museu di a Corsica
musee-de-la-corse-museu-di-a-corsica.description: Set in the Citadel of Corte, a former 15th-century château fortified in the 18th century, this regional museum of anthropology opened in June 1997 in a building designed by the architect Andrea Bruno. It draws on some three thousand objects of traditional Corsica gathered by Father Louis Doazan, a pioneer of the island's ethnography.

musee-de-la-cour-d-or.name: Cour d'Or Museum
musee-de-la-cour-d-or.description: Founded in 1839, the Metz museum took in 1988 the name of the palace of the kings of Austrasia, whose presumed site it occupies. It brings together under one roof rich Gallo-Roman collections, including baths preserved in situ, a museum of medieval and Renaissance architecture, and a fine art gallery.

musee-de-la-creche.name: Nativity Scene Museum
musee-de-la-creche.description: An annexe of the Chaumont Museum of Art and History, it presents a collection of antique nativity scenes acquired by the city in 1976. It includes a monumental group of 18th-century Neapolitan cribs, held to be the finest example preserved in France, whose figurines depict the whole of Neapolitan society.

musee-de-la-deportation-et-de-la-resista.name: Museum of Deportation and Resistance of the Hautes-Pyrénées
musee-de-la-deportation-et-de-la-resista.description: A Tarbes museum devoted to the Second World War in the Hautes-Pyrénées. Its display cases bring together photographs, posters, deportees' uniforms, weapons and objects made in the camps, brought back by former Resistance fighters and deportees; a documentation centre rounds out the visit.

musee-de-la-faience-de-sarreguemines.name: Sarreguemines Faience Museum
musee-de-la-faience-de-sarreguemines.description: Founded in 1923 and at first devoted to local history and traditions, it reopened in 1972 with a focus on the ceramic arts, its collections having been scattered during the war. It occupies the former apartments of the villa of Paul de Geiger, director of the faience works from 1871 to 1913, whose faience salon has been listed as a historic monument since 1979.

musee-de-la-faience-et-des-beaux-arts-fr.name: Frédéric Blandin Museum of Faience and Fine Arts
musee-de-la-faience-et-des-beaux-arts-fr.description: Born in the 1840s and enriched by the patron Frédéric Blandin, the museum reopened on 27 September 2013 in a former Benedictine abbey paired with a contemporary extension. It holds nearly 2,500 pieces of Nevers faience, a group of enamelled spun-glass work unique to Nevers, and paintings by Seurat, Derain and Modigliani.

musee-de-la-figurine-historique.name: Museum of the Historical Figurine
musee-de-la-figurine-historique.description: Born of the bequests of Arthur de Marsy in 1901 and Alfred Ternisien in 1927, it opened in 1984 as the first museum of note devoted to the historical figurine. Its some 30,000 pieces trace armies through the centuries and are staged in dioramas, including Charles Laurent's Waterloo.

musee-de-la-franc-maconnerie.name: Museum of Freemasonry
musee-de-la-franc-maconnerie.description: At the headquarters of the Grand Orient de France on Rue Cadet, this museum recounts three centuries of Freemasonry in France through ritual objects, aprons, lodge regalia and documents linked to celebrated masons such as Voltaire and La Fayette.

musee-de-la-gendarmerie.name: National Gendarmerie Museum
musee-de-la-gendarmerie.description: The national museum of the French Gendarmerie, opened in 2015 beside the officers' academy in Melun, retraces the force's history from the medieval maréchaussée to today through uniforms, weapons, vehicles and archives.

musee-de-la-grande-guerre.name: Museum of the Great War
musee-de-la-grande-guerre.description: Opened in 2011 on the edge of the First Battle of the Marne battlefield, this museum holds one of Europe's largest First World War collections, some 70,000 objects and documents built around collector Jean-Pierre Verney's holdings.

musee-de-la-grande-loge-de-france.name: Museum of the Grande Loge de France
musee-de-la-grande-loge-de-france.description: Housed in the Grande Loge de France's headquarters, a former Franciscan convent in the 17th arrondissement, this museum of the history, symbols and art of Freemasonry preserves over 3,000 objects dating from the 18th century onwards.

musee-de-la-liberation-de-paris-musee-du.name: Museum of the Liberation of Paris
musee-de-la-liberation-de-paris-musee-du.description: Reinstalled in 2019 in the Ledoux pavilions at Denfert-Rochereau, this City of Paris museum recounts the Occupation and the liberation of Paris through General Leclerc and Jean Moulin, and includes Colonel Rol-Tanguy's underground command post of August 1944.

musee-de-la-liberation-fort-du-roule.name: Fort du Roule
musee-de-la-liberation-fort-du-roule.description: A fort built between 1853 and 1857 under Napoleon III atop Mont du Roule, turned by the Germans into an entrenched camp with underground galleries and recaptured by the Americans from 25 to 27 June 1944. It has housed the Cherbourg Liberation Museum since 1954.

musee-de-la-maille-mode-et-industrie-hot.name: Museum of Knitwear, Fashion and Industry – Hôtel de Vauluisant
musee-de-la-maille-mode-et-industrie-hot.description: Set in the Hôtel de Vauluisant, a Renaissance mansion in the centre of Troyes, this museum traces the story of Troyes hosiery-making, which made the city a European capital of knitwear. Wooden looms, refined machinery, stockings, socks and underwear tell two centuries of textile craft.

musee-de-la-mer-sete.name: Museum of the Sea
musee-de-la-mer-sete.description: Opened in May 2014 between the Théâtre de la Mer and the seaside cemetery, in a building of clean lines paying homage to the style of the 1920s. It tells the story of the port of Sète since the 18th century and of Languedoc water-jousting, and displays the collection of fishing-boat models made by the shipwright André Aversa.

musee-de-la-moto.name: Motorcycle Museum
musee-de-la-moto.description: Set in the Merlan district, this Marseille museum traces the history of the motorcycle. It lines up machines and sidecars from the 19th century to the 1990s, including an unrestored 1904 Motosacoche with a Dufaux engine and a 600cc MGC prototype, and holds a library of specialist magazines.

musee-de-la-musique.name: Music Museum
musee-de-la-musique.description: The Philharmonie de Paris's instrument museum at La Villette displays around 1,000 pieces from a collection of more than 8,000 — Stradivarius violins, harpsichords, rare guitars — covering five centuries of European and world music.

musee-de-la-photographie-charles-negre.name: Charles Nègre Museum of Photography
musee-de-la-photographie-charles-negre.description: Opened in 2016 at the heart of Vieux-Nice, it occupies a former electrical substation commissioned in the 1930s, whose industrial character it has retained. Named after the painter and photographer Charles Nègre (1820–1880), a pioneer of photography, it programmes monographic exhibitions and regional photographic creation.

musee-de-la-poste.name: Postal Museum
musee-de-la-poste.description: The museum of the French postal service, near Montparnasse, reopened in 2019 after full renovation. Its collections range from mail coaches, uniforms and postboxes to the airmail epic and one of France's leading philatelic collections.

musee-de-la-prefecture-de-police.name: Museum of the Paris Police Prefecture
musee-de-la-prefecture-de-police.description: Tucked inside a working police station in the Latin Quarter, this museum traces the history of the Paris police from the 17th century onwards, with archives, uniforms, weapons and evidence from celebrated criminal cases.

musee-de-la-princerie.name: Princerie Museum
musee-de-la-princerie.description: The museum occupies the Hôtel de la Princerie, residence of the princier, the diocese's highest-ranking dignitary after the bishop, rebuilt in Renaissance style in 1525 by the Musson brothers. Badly damaged during the First World War, the mansion was bought by the city in 1926, which in 1932 installed there the collections assembled since 1822.

musee-de-la-reddition-du-7-mai-1945.name: Museum of the Surrender of 7 May 1945
musee-de-la-reddition-du-7-mai-1945.description: Founded in 1985 for the fortieth anniversary of the event, the museum occupies part of the former Collège Moderne et Technique of Reims, later the Lycée Franklin-Roosevelt, where Eisenhower set up the Allied headquarters in February 1945. The map room, where the German surrender was signed on 7 May 1945 at 2:41 a.m., is listed as a historic monument.

musee-de-la-renaissance-chateau-d-ecouen.name: National Museum of the Renaissance
musee-de-la-renaissance-chateau-d-ecouen.description: France's national Renaissance museum fills the 16th-century château built for Constable Anne de Montmorency north of Paris. Its collections include the ten-piece David and Bathsheba tapestry cycle, enamels, ceramics and painted fireplaces.

musee-de-la-renaissance-en-champagne-hot.name: Museum of the Renaissance in Champagne – Hôtel de Vauluisant
musee-de-la-renaissance-en-champagne-hot.description: Set in the Hôtel de Vauluisant, a Renaissance mansion in Troyes, it is devoted to 16th-century Champagne. Sculptures of the renowned Troyes school, stained glass and paintings bear witness to the artistic influence of Champagne during this period.

musee-de-la-resistance-de-limoges.name: Limoges Museum of the Resistance and Deportation
musee-de-la-resistance-de-limoges.description: Set in the former convent of the Sisters of Providence, built from the 17th century and enlarged in the 18th by the architect Joseph Brousseau, at the heart of the Cité district. Entirely renovated and enlarged between 2009 and 2012, it traces the history of the Resistance, the Occupation and deportation in the Limousin.

musee-de-la-resistance-et-de-la-deportat.name: Isère Museum of the Resistance and Deportation
musee-de-la-resistance-et-de-la-deportat.description: Opened on 23 April 1966 on the initiative of former Resistance fighters and deportees, the departmental museum moved in 1994 to rue Hébert, into a refurbished building of 1863. More than 5,000 posters, photographs, printed matter and personal objects there recount the entry into resistance, the maquis, the persecution of Jews, repression and the Liberation in the Isère.

musee-de-la-resistance-et-du-combattant.name: Montauban Museum of the Resistance and Combatants
musee-de-la-resistance-et-du-combattant.description: Created by the city of Montauban in 1989 following a gift from a former Resistance deportee, it occupies the Espace Perbosc. Devoted at first to the 1939–45 conflict in France and Tarn-et-Garonne, it broadened in 2014, with new staging, to the conflicts of the 20th and 21st centuries.

musee-de-la-resistance-nationale.name: National Resistance Museum
musee-de-la-resistance-nationale.description: This museum in Champigny-sur-Marne holds one of the largest collections devoted to the French Resistance — underground newspapers, leaflets, weapons and personal effects — displayed since 2020 in the new Aimé Césaire building.

musee-de-la-romanite.name: Museum of Romanity
musee-de-la-romanite.description: Opened on 2 June 2018 opposite the amphitheatre, in a building by Elizabeth de Portzamparc clad in a pleated glass façade evoking a toga. It presents Nîmes' archaeological collections, from Gaulish origins to Roman daily life and the legacy of Romanity, supported by sixty-five multimedia displays.

musee-de-la-tapisserie-de-bayeux.name: Bayeux Tapestry Museum
musee-de-la-tapisserie-de-bayeux.description: An 11th-century embroidery nearly 70 metres long, it recounts the conquest of England by William, Duke of Normandy, up to the Battle of Hastings in 1066, and has been listed on UNESCO's Memory of the World register since 2007. It is displayed in the former grand seminary of Bayeux, built from 1693, now the Centre Guillaume-le-Conquérant.

musee-de-la-toile-de-jouy.name: Toile de Jouy Museum
musee-de-la-toile-de-jouy.description: Housed in the Château de l'Églantine, this museum tells the story of toile de Jouy, the printed cottons made at the Oberkampf manufactory founded in Jouy-en-Josas in 1760, through fabrics, printing plates and period costume.

musee-de-la-tour-aux-puces.name: Tour aux Puces Museum
musee-de-la-tour-aux-puces.description: A former fourteen-sided polygonal keep of the counts of Luxembourg, built in the 11th–12th centuries, the Tour aux Puces owes its name to a corruption of the Luxembourgish 'Peetzturm'. Reopened in 2001 after restoration, it houses Thionville's museum of archaeology and history, from prehistory to the Renaissance, across eight themed rooms.

musee-de-la-venerie.name: Museum of Venery
musee-de-la-venerie.description: Set in the prior's lodging of the Saint-Maurice priory, founded by Saint Louis in 1264 within the grounds of the royal château of Senlis, this museum is devoted to venery, the hunt with hounds. Its collections bring together paintings, engravings, trophies and works of art evoking this tradition and the royal forests of the Oise.

musee-de-la-vie-bourguignonne-perrin-de-.name: Perrin de Puycousin Museum of Burgundian Life
musee-de-la-vie-bourguignonne-perrin-de-.description: A museum of regional ethnography founded in 1938 from the collection of Maurice Perrin de Puycousin, housed since 1984 in the former Bernardine monastery, a 17th-century building. It evokes rural and urban Burgundian life through costumes, tools, reconstructed Dijon shops, and a section devoted to mustard.

musee-de-la-vie-romantique.name: Museum of Romantic Life
musee-de-la-vie-romantique.description: The 1830 house and studio of painter Ary Scheffer, in the 'New Athens' quarter at the foot of Montmartre, evokes the Romantic era with George Sand memorabilia, works by Scheffer and his circle, and a garden tearoom.

musee-de-melun.name: Melun Museum
musee-de-melun.description: Melun's museum of art and history, founded in 1860 and housed in the 16th-century Hôtel de la Vicomté. It presents Gallo-Roman and medieval finds from the town alongside paintings and a large body of work by sculptor Henri Chapu.

musee-de-mirecourt.name: Mirecourt Museum
musee-de-mirecourt.description: Devoted to French violin- and bow-making, of which Mirecourt is the birthplace, this museum, opened in 1973, occupies a former drying shed for lutherie wood on the banks of the Madon. It holds more than three hundred bowed and plucked string instruments, as well as workshop tools, raw materials and archives.

musee-de-montmartre.name: Montmartre Museum
musee-de-montmartre.description: Set in one of the hill's oldest houses, where Renoir, Suzanne Valadon and Utrillo lived or worked, the museum traces Montmartre's bohemian era through paintings and cabaret posters, with Valadon's recreated studio and gardens above the Clos Montmartre vineyard.

musee-de-normandie.name: Normandy Museum
musee-de-normandie.description: Founded in 1946 on the initiative of the historian Michel de Boüard, this museum of history and society has been housed since 1963 in the Logis des Gouverneurs, a 14th-century building within the grounds of Caen Castle. Its collections trace the history of Normandy, from prehistory to the 20th century.

musee-de-picardie.name: Picardy Museum
musee-de-picardie.description: Built from 1855 to 1867 by the architect Henri Parent, it is the first building in France designed specifically to house a fine art museum. Opened in 1869 with the collections of the Société des Antiquaires de Picardie, it brings together archaeology, old master painting, and the great mural decorations by Puvis de Chavannes.

musee-de-port-royal-des-champs.name: Museum of Port-Royal des Champs
musee-de-port-royal-des-champs.description: National museum on the site of the ruined abbey of Port-Royal-des-Champs, centre of 17th-century Jansenism linked to Pascal and Racine. The former Petites Écoles display paintings by Philippe de Champaigne and relics of the community, amid the abbey grounds.

musee-de-prehistoire-d-ile-de-france.name: Île-de-France Museum of Prehistory
musee-de-prehistoire-d-ile-de-france.description: Departmental museum of the region's prehistory, in a raw-concrete building by architect Roland Simounet on the edge of Nemours forest. Displays run from the Palaeolithic to the Iron Age, with finds from major Seine valley sites such as Pincevent and Étiolles.

musee-de-prehistoire-de-terra-amata.name: Terra Amata
musee-de-prehistoire-de-terra-amata.description: A prehistory museum built on an open-air site discovered on the slopes of Mont Boron and occupied around 400,000 years ago. Excavations there yielded Acheulean tools and one of the oldest confirmed hearths in Europe, a key piece of evidence for dating the domestication of fire.

musee-de-prehistoire-regionale-de-menton.name: Menton Museum of Regional Prehistory
musee-de-prehistoire-regionale-de-menton.description: Opened in 1909 in a building erected for it, this municipal museum was entirely rethought in 1988 by the prehistorian Henry de Lumley. It presents the prehistory of the region and of Liguria, from tools of the Grotte du Vallonnet, more than a million years old, through to the Iron Age.

musee-de-provins-et-du-provinois.name: Museum of Provins and the Provinois
musee-de-provins-et-du-provinois.description: Local museum of the medieval fair town of Provins, a UNESCO World Heritage site, housed in the Maison Romane, one of its oldest houses. Its collections span prehistory to the 19th century, from medieval sculpture and glazed floor tiles to religious treasures.

musee-de-saint-antoine-l-abbaye.name: Saint-Antoine-l'Abbaye Museum
musee-de-saint-antoine-l-abbaye.description: Created in 1979 by the department of Isère, this museum occupies the former novitiate of the Antonine abbey, rebuilt in the 17th and 18th centuries on medieval foundations. It traces the history of this hospitaller order and major pilgrimage site, and holds a collection bequeathed by the painter Jean Vinay.

musee-de-saint-maur-villa-medicis.name: Villa Médicis – House of Arts and Culture
musee-de-saint-maur-villa-medicis.description: Saint-Maur's art and history museum, in an old house renamed 'Villa Médicis' after Catherine de' Medici's stays at the town's château. It keeps carved stones from the medieval abbey, paintings and prints, and a major collection of Art Deco ceramicist Édouard Cazaux.

musee-de-tesse.name: Tessé Museum
musee-de-tesse.description: Opened to the public in 1799, making Le Mans one of the first cities in France to have a museum, it has occupied the former episcopal palace, built in the 19th century, since 1927. It brings together Italian primitives, 17th-century French painting, and an Egyptian section with reconstructed tombs of Nefertari and Sennefer.

musee-de-valence-art-et-archeologie.name: Valence Museum of Art and Archaeology
musee-de-valence-art-et-archeologie.description: A museum founded in 1850, set in the former episcopal palace of Valence, remodelled in the 18th century. Enlarged by the architect Jean-Paul Philippon and reopened in 2013, it spreads across thirty-five rooms bringing together regional archaeology, decorative arts and paintings, including an exceptional group of drawings and paintings by Hubert Robert.

musee-de-vire-normandie.name: Vire Normandie Museum
musee-de-vire-normandie.description: Founded in 1866 in the wake of Arcisse de Caumont and then destroyed by the bombing of 1944, the museum reopened in 1956 in the former hôtel-Dieu, a classical 18th-century building. Its collections combine archaeology, fine arts, ethnography and industry to tell the story of the Norman Bocage.

musee-denys-puech.name: Denys-Puech Fine Arts Museum
musee-denys-puech.description: Created in 1910 on the initiative of the sculptor Denys Puech, who gave Rodez a substantial body of studio work, the museum occupies a building designed by the architect André Boyer. It holds nearly 1,400 works: sculptures by Puech, paintings by the Orientalist Maurice Bompard, engravings by Eugène Viala, and contemporary art besides.

musee-departemental-albert-kahn.name: Albert Kahn Museum
musee-departemental-albert-kahn.description: Museum of banker-philanthropist Albert Kahn's 'Archives of the Planet', some 72,000 early colour photographs taken around the world between 1909 and 1931. Its Kengo Kuma-designed building opens onto four hectares of gardens with Japanese, English and French scenes.

musee-departemental-arles-antique.name: Museum of Ancient Arles
musee-departemental-arles-antique.description: Nicknamed 'the Blue Museum', this departmental museum, designed by the architect Henri Ciriani, opened in 1995 on the peninsula once occupied by the Roman circus, and gained an extension in 2012. It brings together Arles' archaeological collections: mosaics, early Christian sarcophagi, and the Gallo-Roman barge Arles-Rhône 3, raised from the river in 2011.

musee-departemental-breton.name: Breton Departmental Museum
musee-departemental-breton.description: Founded in 1846 by the Société Archéologique du Finistère, the museum occupies the former palace of the bishops of Cornouaille, whose Renaissance-style Tour de Rohan was begun in 1508. It presents archaeology, Breton costumes, furniture and wood sculpture, as well as an extensive collection of Quimper faience.

musee-departemental-henri-matisse.name: Matisse Museum
musee-departemental-henri-matisse.description: The only museum created by Henri Matisse during his lifetime, opened on 8 November 1952 in his home town with an initial gift of 82 works. Housed since 1982 in the Palais Fénelon, a former 18th-century episcopal palace, it also holds the Herbin and Tériade donations.

musee-departemental-maurice-denis.name: Maurice Denis Museum
musee-departemental-maurice-denis.description: Museum of painter Maurice Denis and the Nabis, in the Priory, a 17th-century former royal hospital Denis bought in 1914 and lived in until his death. It shows works by Denis, Sérusier, Bonnard and their circle, the chapel he decorated, and terraced gardens.

musee-departemental-stephane-mallarme.name: Stéphane Mallarmé Museum
musee-departemental-stephane-mallarme.description: The riverside house facing the Fontainebleau forest where poet Stéphane Mallarmé spent his summers from 1874 and died in 1898. His furnished rooms, personal belongings, portraits and manuscripts are preserved, along with a garden replanted as in his day.

musee-des-ameriques-auch.name: Museum of the Americas – Auch
musee-des-ameriques-auch.description: A municipal museum born in 1793, housed since 1976 in the former Jacobin convent founded in 1386 and remodelled in the 17th century. It holds France's second-largest public collection of pre-Columbian art, originating from the bequest of Guillaume Pujos, an Auch tailor who emigrated to Chile, and considerably enriched since by the Lions donation.

musee-des-annees-trente.name: Museum of the 1930s
musee-des-annees-trente.description: Museum of art and design from the interwar years: figurative painting, sculpture, Art Deco furniture and models of the modernist villas built in Boulogne-Billancourt by Le Corbusier, Mallet-Stevens and Perret. It is part of the Espace Landowski cultural complex.

musee-des-antiquites.name: Museum of Antiquities
musee-des-antiquites.description: Created in 1831 to house the finds from the Lillebonne excavations, this departmental museum occupies the former Visitation convent, built from 1680 to 1691. It holds Gallo-Roman and medieval collections, including the Lillebonne mosaic and the Winged Stags tapestry, as well as an Egyptian collection.
