musee-des-archives-nationales-hotel-de-s.name: Museum of the National Archives – Hôtel de Soubise
musee-des-archives-nationales-hotel-de-s.description: Museum of the French National Archives in the Hôtel de Soubise, a princely Marais mansion with rococo apartments decorated by Germain Boffrand. Its rotating displays present landmark documents of French history, from royal wills to Marie-Antoinette's last letter.

musee-des-arts-asiatiques-guimet.name: Guimet Museum
musee-des-arts-asiatiques-guimet.description: France's national museum of Asian arts, founded by industrialist Émile Guimet in 1889 and holding one of the largest Asian collections outside Asia: Khmer sculpture, Chinese bronzes and porcelain, Japanese screens, Indian and Himalayan art.

musee-des-arts-asiatiques-maa.name: Museum of Asian Arts (MAA)
musee-des-arts-asiatiques-maa.description: Housed since 2000 in the Villa Jules-Verne, in Le Mourillon facing the sea, this municipal museum presents the city's collections of Asian art, assembled through collectors' gifts and bequests. The rooms are organised by geographic area: China and Japan, then South-East Asia, India, Mongolia and Tibet.

musee-des-arts-d-afrique-et-d-asie.name: Museum of the Arts of Africa and Asia
musee-des-arts-d-afrique-et-d-asie.description: Founded in 1923 by Father Henri Watthé, a Lazarist missionary, this museum occupies an 1881 building that once housed a hydrotherapy establishment and later the Vichy water-testing laboratory. Its collections, born of missionaries' gifts, bring together African ritual objects and masks and the arts of East and South-East Asia.

musee-des-arts-decoratifs-strasbourg.name: Strasbourg Museum of Decorative Arts
musee-des-arts-decoratifs-strasbourg.description: Set on the ground floor of the Palais Rohan, a former residence of the prince-bishops built from 1732 to 1742 to designs by Robert de Cotte, the museum brings together the sumptuous apartments of the Rohan cardinals and Strasbourg's decorative arts collections from the 17th to the 19th century, including the famous faience and porcelain of the Hannong manufactory.

musee-des-arts-decoratifs-union-centrale.name: Museum of Decorative Arts
musee-des-arts-decoratifs-union-centrale.description: Decorative arts and design museum in the Rivoli wing of the Louvre palace, covering furniture, glass, ceramics, wallpaper, graphic design and fashion from the Middle Ages to today, with period rooms and strong Art Nouveau and Art Deco holdings.

musee-des-arts-et-metiers.name: Museum of Arts and Crafts
musee-des-arts-et-metiers.description: Technology museum founded in 1794 with the Conservatoire des arts et métiers, partly housed in a former medieval priory. Its instruments, machines and vehicles include Foucault's pendulum, Lavoisier's laboratory and Ader's and Blériot's early aeroplanes.

musee-des-arts-et-traditions-populaires-.name: Wattrelos Museum of Popular Arts and Traditions
musee-des-arts-et-traditions-populaires-.description: Set in a former square-courtyard farm, also known as a cense, this municipal museum evokes everyday life of around one hundred and fifty years ago. Objects are presented as staged scenes recreating in detail the work, home life and leisure of the 19th century.

musee-des-arts-precieux-paul-dupuy.name: Paul Dupuy Museum of Precious Arts
musee-des-arts-precieux-paul-dupuy.description: The collector Paul Dupuy bought this mansion on rue de la Pleau in 1909 and restored it; he bequeathed the building and its collections, which became a municipal museum in 1949. Devoted to precious and graphic arts, it holds clocks and watches from the 16th to 19th centuries, medieval ivories, Toulouse goldsmith's work, and several thousand drawings and prints.

musee-des-augustins.name: Augustins Museum of Toulouse
musee-des-augustins.description: One of the oldest museums in France, founded in 1793 and opened in 1795, it occupies the former Augustinian convent, begun in 1310 and consecrated in 1504, restored in the 19th century under Viollet-le-Duc. It holds paintings from the 14th to the 19th century and a major collection of Romanesque and Gothic sculpture.

musee-des-avelines-musee-d-art-et-d-hist.name: Musée des Avelines – Saint-Cloud Museum of Art and History
musee-des-avelines-musee-d-art-et-d-hist.description: Saint-Cloud's museum of art and history, in a 1930s villa inspired by the Villa Kérylos. Its collections recall the royal château that burned in 1870, the town's 18th-century soft-paste porcelain manufactory, and local painters and sculptors.

musee-des-beaux-arts-d-angers.name: Angers Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-d-angers.description: Founded in 1801 on the model of the Louvre and then made municipal in 1805, the museum occupies the Logis Barrault, a mansion from the late 15th century. Its collections span the 14th to the 20th century, with a rich body of 18th-century French painting and more than 13,000 drawings.

musee-des-beaux-arts-d-orleans.name: Orléans Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-d-orleans.description: Founded in 1797, it is one of the oldest provincial museums; it has occupied a building by the architect Christian Langlois, next to the town hall, since 1984. With 2,000 paintings and 10,000 drawings, it holds France's second-largest collection of pastels after the Louvre's.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-bordeaux.name: Bordeaux Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-bordeaux.description: Born of the Chaptal decree of 1801, the museum occupies two wings built from 1875 by the architect Charles Burguet, on either side of the town hall garden. Its some 2,300 paintings span the 15th to the 20th century, with a 17th-century Dutch collection among the most important in France.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-caen.name: Caen Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-caen.description: Founded in 1801 and opened in 1809, the museum was entirely destroyed in the bombing of 1944 and reopened in 1970 within the grounds of Caen's ducal castle. It is renowned for its Italian, Flemish and French paintings of the 16th and 17th centuries and for the print collection assembled by Bernard Mancel.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-calais.name: Calais Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-calais.description: Opened in 1966 in a building by the architect Paul Pamart, the museum originally brought together fine art and lace, before the lace collection moved to another site in 2009. It holds Flemish and Dutch paintings, including works by Gerrit van Honthorst and Frans Snyders, and modern French works.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-carcassonne.name: Carcassonne Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-carcassonne.description: Set in the former présidial (royal court), whose present façade was completed in 1900, the museum was founded in 1836 by enthusiasts of art and archaeology. Its collections, from the 16th to the 20th century, include paintings by Chardin, Corot and Courbet, and a substantial body of work by the Carcassonne-born painter Jacques Gamelin.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-chambery.name: Chambéry Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-chambery.description: Set in a former grain hall raised in 1889 by the architect François Pelaz, the museum reopened in 2012 after lengthy renovation. Built up through the bequests of Savoyard collectors, its collection of Italian paintings is the third-largest in France, spanning the Trecento to the Florentine and Neapolitan Baroque schools.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-chartres.name: Chartres Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-chartres.description: Founded in 1833, the museum has been housed since 1939 in the former episcopal palace, listed as a historic monument in 1906, whose buildings date from the 13th, 17th and 18th centuries. It holds Renaissance and 18th-century paintings, Léonard Limosin's series of enamel apostles, and Oceanic collections.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-dijon.name: Dijon Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-dijon.description: Founded by decree in 1787 and opened in 1799, it is one of the oldest museums in France; it occupies the Palace of the Dukes and Estates of Burgundy, remodelled in the 17th century to plans by Jules Hardouin-Mansart. The Salle des Gardes there houses the tombs of the dukes of Burgundy.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-dole.name: Dole Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-dole.description: Founded in 1821 by the mayor Dusillet and the sculptor Jean-Séraphin-Désiré Besson, the museum has occupied the Pavillon des Officiers, an example of 18th-century Franche-Comté military architecture, since 1980. It brings together regional archaeology, French, Italian and Nordic paintings from the 17th to the 19th century, and a collection of Figuration Narrative art.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-libourne.name: Libourne Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-libourne.description: Founded in 1818 on the initiative of the Duke Élie Decazes, then Minister of the Interior and a native of the region, the museum occupies the second floor of the town hall, a building originally dating from the 15th century. Its rooms present European painting from the 14th to the 20th century, including works by Rubens and Cranach.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-limoges-bal-pala.name: Limoges Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-limoges-bal-pala.description: Opened in 1912 in the former episcopal palace built from 1766 to 1774 by the architect Joseph Brousseau, the museum overlooks the Évêché gardens. It holds one of the richest collections of Limoges enamels, from the Middle Ages to the present, paintings by Renoir, who was born in the city, and an Egyptian collection.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-lons-le-saunier.name: Lons-le-Saunier Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-lons-le-saunier.description: Founded in 1817 and set in a wing of the town hall on place Philibert-de-Chalon, the museum presents on the ground floor works by the sculptor Jean-Joseph Perraud (1819–1876), who bequeathed part of his output to it. The upper floor brings together some thirty paintings of the French, Nordic and Italian schools, including a Courbet.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-lyon.name: Lyon Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-lyon.description: Set in the former Abbey of the Ladies of Saint-Pierre, known as the Palais Saint-Pierre, the museum was born of the Chaptal decree of 1801 and opened in 1803. Its seventy rooms range from antiquity to modern art, with the Venetian Renaissance, a Rembrandt, a Gauguin, and the Jacqueline Delubac bequest.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-marseille.name: Marseille Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-marseille.description: Founded in 1802 following the Chaptal decree, the museum has occupied a wing of the Palais Longchamp, a building opened in 1869 to designs by the architect Henry Espérandieu, since 1873. It holds paintings, sculptures and drawings from the 16th to the 19th century, including a major group of sculptures by Pierre Puget.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-mulhouse.name: Mulhouse Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-mulhouse.description: Founded in 1864 by the industrialist Frédéric Engel-Dollfus and the Société Industrielle de Mulhouse, the museum occupies the Villa Steinbach, a residence built in 1788 for a manufacturer, and has been devoted to fine art since 1964. Its collections range from the late Middle Ages to contemporary art, with a substantial body of work by Jean-Jacques Henner.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-nancy.name: Nancy Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-nancy.description: Founded in 1793 from works seized during the Revolution, the museum has occupied a pavilion built in the 18th century by Emmanuel Héré on place Stanislas since 1936, enlarged with a contemporary wing in 1999. Its 40,000 works cover European painting from the 14th to the 20th century and an extensive collection of Daum glassware.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-nimes.name: Nîmes Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-nimes.description: Founded in 1821 in the Maison Carrée, the museum moved in 1907 into a building by the Nîmes-born architect Max Raphel, refitted by Jean-Michel Wilmotte in 1987. It holds around 3,800 works from the 14th to the 19th century, arranged around a large Roman mosaic depicting the marriage of Admetus.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-pau.name: Pau Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-pau.description: Founded in 1864 on the initiative of the Société des Amis des Arts de Pau, the museum has occupied a building constructed for it by the architect Jacques Ruillier since 1931. Its collections cover the European schools from the 16th to the 20th century and are arranged around Edgar Degas's A Cotton Office in New Orleans.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-rennes.name: Rennes Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-rennes.description: Set in the former university palace on the quai Émile-Zola, the museum was formed from the revolutionary seizures of 1794 and the cabinet of curiosities of the Marquis de Robien. It holds European paintings from the 14th to the 20th century, including Georges de La Tour's The Newborn, and a graphic arts collection of international standing.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-rouen.name: Rouen Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-rouen.description: Created by the Chaptal decree of 1801, it ranks among the richest museums in France. The present building, erected by the architect Louis Sauvageot from 1877, spreads paintings, sculptures and graphic art across some sixty rooms, from Caravaggio's Flagellation of Christ to the Impressionists.

musee-des-beaux-arts-de-tours.name: Tours Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-de-tours.description: Set in the former archbishop's palace beside the cathedral, the museum grew from works seized during the Revolution, with a first display opening to the public in 1795. Its collections range from antiquity to contemporary art, including two panels by Andrea Mantegna; the listed site preserves a formal French garden and a cedar of Lebanon.

musee-des-beaux-arts-et-d-archeologie-de.name: Besançon Museum of Fine Arts and Archaeology
musee-des-beaux-arts-et-d-archeologie-de.description: Founded in 1694 thanks to the bequest of the abbé Jean-Baptiste Boisot, it is the oldest public museum in France, predating the Louvre by a century. Set in the former grain hall by Pierre Marnotte, it was refitted from 1967 to 1970 by Louis Miquel, a pupil of Le Corbusier, and then entirely renovated in 2018.

musee-des-beaux-arts-et-d-archeologie-de.name: Châlons-en-Champagne Museum of Fine Arts and Archaeology
musee-des-beaux-arts-et-d-archeologie-de.description: Created in 1794 as the departmental museum to receive the property of émigrés and religious houses, it occupies a building on place Godart whose pediments are the work of the sculptor Gustave Navlet (1890–91). Old master paintings, Limoges enamels, sculptures by Rodin and medieval archaeology sit side by side there.

musee-des-beaux-arts-et-d-archeologie-de.name: Vienne Museum of Fine Arts and Archaeology
musee-des-beaux-arts-et-d-archeologie-de.description: Opened to the public in 1895 in a former grain hall at the heart of the town, it is one of five heritage sites managed by Vienne. Its collections span the Neolithic to the present day, combining archaeology unearthed from Vienne's soil with decorative arts and painting.

musee-des-beaux-arts-et-de-la-dentelle-d.name: Alençon Museum of Fine Arts and Lace
musee-des-beaux-arts-et-de-la-dentelle-d.description: Founded in 1857 and set in part of the former Jesuit college, the museum presents point d'Alençon, a needle lace inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010. It also holds paintings from the 16th to the 20th century and a Cambodian collection assembled by Adhémard Leclère.

musee-des-beaux-arts-jules-cheret.name: Jules Chéret Fine Arts Museum
musee-des-beaux-arts-jules-cheret.description: The museum occupies a villa inspired by the Italian Renaissance, begun in 1878 for Princess Elizabeth Kochubey and completed for the Thompson family. Acquired by the city in 1925, it opened as a museum in 1928 and houses collections built up through successive donations, including a substantial group of works by Jules Chéret.

musee-des-confluences.name: Musée des Confluences
musee-des-confluences.description: Opened in 2014 at the southern tip of the Presqu'île, where the Rhône and Saône meet, in a Deconstructivist building by the Vienna firm Coop Himmelb(l)au. Successor to Lyon's Guimet natural history museum, it brings together natural science, anthropology and the history of societies.

musee-des-cultures-taurines.name: Museum of Bullfighting Cultures
musee-des-cultures-taurines.description: Opened in 2002 for the fiftieth anniversary of the Nîmes feria, in the former Crédit Municipal, an early 20th-century building arranged around a patio. It brings together more than 30,000 pieces from the old Nîmes museum and the collections of Henriette and Claude Viallat, devoted to the Camargue and Spanish bullfighting traditions.

musee-des-docks-romains.name: Roman Docks Museum
musee-des-docks-romains.description: Created in 1963 on remains uncovered in 1947 during the reconstruction of the Vieux-Port districts, it presents in situ one of the few known Roman commercial warehouses in the world. Some thirty dolia — large jars able to hold nearly 2,000 litres of wine — are preserved there in their original location.

musee-des-explorations-du-monde-ancien-m.name: Museum of World Explorations (former Musée de la Castre)
musee-des-explorations-du-monde-ancien-m.description: Set in the château built from the 11th century by the monks of Lérins atop Le Suquet, the museum was born in 1877 from the donation of the Dutch baron Tinco Lycklama à Nijeholt. It brings together Mediterranean antiquities and the arts of Oceania, the Arctic, the Himalayas and pre-Columbian America, around a medieval watchtower.

musee-des-impressionnismes-giverny.name: Museum of Impressionisms Giverny
musee-des-impressionnismes-giverny.description: Opened in 2009 within the walls of the former Museum of American Art, active from 1992 to 2008, it stands a few steps from Claude Monet's house and gardens. Devoted to Impressionism, its sources and its legacy, it presents temporary exhibitions each season.

musee-des-monnaies-et-medailles.name: Museum of the Monnaie de Paris (11 Conti)
musee-des-monnaies-et-medailles.description: Museum of the Monnaie de Paris — the French mint, founded in 864 — inside its 18th-century neoclassical palace on the Quai de Conti. The '11 Conti' circuit displays coins, medals and presses, and looks into workshops where craftsmen still strike medals today.

musee-des-monnaies-et-medailles-joseph-p.name: Joseph Puig Museum of Coins and Medals
musee-des-monnaies-et-medailles-joseph-p.description: A numismatic museum set in the Villa Les Tilleuls, bequeathed to Perpignan along with its collection by the merchant Joseph Puig (1859–1929). Opened in 1984, it covers nearly twenty-five centuries of monetary history and places particular emphasis on Catalan coinage; the donor's study has been recreated there.

musee-des-monuments-francais.name: Museum of French Monuments
musee-des-monuments-francais.description: Within the Cité de l'architecture et du patrimoine at the Palais de Chaillot, this museum conceived by Viollet-le-Duc assembles life-size casts of portals and sculpture from French cathedrals and châteaux, together with copies of medieval wall paintings.

musee-des-moulins-jean-bruggeman.name: Jean Bruggeman Windmill Museum
musee-des-moulins-jean-bruggeman.description: Created by the regional association of windmill enthusiasts and opened in 1995, the museum is set beside two windmills re-erected on the site, including the Moulin des Olieux, an oil mill built in Flanders in 1743. It traces the history of milling, from Neolithic querns to modern roller mills, and the trades attached to it.

musee-des-papillons.name: Butterfly Museum
musee-des-papillons.description: Set in the Espace Saint-Jacques, the museum holds a substantial entomological collection of some 600,000 specimens, assembled over more than a century. Butterflies and beetles, displayed in period cases and boxes, sit alongside other insects, arachnids, and jars of reptiles and amphibians.

musee-des-pays-de-seine-et-marne.name: Museum of the Seine-et-Marne Countryside
musee-des-pays-de-seine-et-marne.description: Departmental museum of rural life in Seine-et-Marne: farm tools, trades and popular traditions of the Brie countryside, with a section devoted to the writer Pierre Mac Orlan, who lived in Saint-Cyr-sur-Morin until his death in 1970.

musee-des-plans-reliefs.name: Museum of Relief Maps
musee-des-plans-reliefs.description: Under the roof of the Hôtel des Invalides, this museum preserves the collection of relief maps of fortified towns begun for Louis XIV in 1668: minutely detailed scale models once used to plan sieges and defences along France's frontiers.

musee-des-spahis.name: Spahis Museum
musee-des-spahis.description: A military museum devoted to the spahis, light cavalry of the Army of Africa, two regiments of which were garrisoned at Senlis from 1928 to 1939 and again from 1948 to 1962. Set since 1991 in a house at the entrance to the royal château, it owes most of its collections to Le Burnous, the association of former spahis.

musee-des-tapisseries.name: Tapestry Museum
musee-des-tapisseries.description: Set in the former archiepiscopal palace of Aix, built between 1650 and 1730, the museum holds hangings from the royal Beauvais manufactory: the Grotesques after Monnoyer, the History of Don Quixote after Natoire, and Russian Games after Le Prince. It also presents costumes and set models from the Aix Festival.

musee-des-transports-urbains-interurbain.name: Museum of Urban, Interurban and Rural Transport (AMTUIR)
musee-des-transports-urbains-interurbain.description: Volunteer-run museum of the AMTUIR association preserving over a century of French public transport: horse-drawn omnibuses, trams, trolleybuses, buses and metro cars kept in a large depot in Chelles, shown during open days and heritage events.

musee-des-troupes-de-montagne.name: Museum of Mountain Troops
musee-des-troupes-de-montagne.description: Created in 1988 for the centenary of the Alpine troops, the museum has occupied the casemated rooms of the Fort de la Bastille, above Grenoble, since 2009. Weapons, uniforms, equipment and reconstructed scenes trace the history of the chasseurs alpins, nicknamed the 'blue devils' since the First World War.

musee-des-ursulines.name: Ursulines Museum
musee-des-ursulines.description: Set since 1968 in the former Ursuline convent, built from 1675 to 1680, turned into a prison during the Revolution and then a barracks until 1929. Its rooms present the prehistory and archaeology of the Mâcon area, a fine art gallery, and a space devoted to the poet Alphonse de Lamartine.

musee-dobree.name: Thomas Dobrée Museum
musee-dobree.description: A Neo-Romanesque palace built from 1862 to 1898 for the Nantes collector Thomas Dobrée, the museum opened in 1899 after his collections were bequeathed to the department. It holds around 135,000 works: medieval manuscripts, Egyptian antiquities brought back by Frédéric Cailliaud, and the reliquary of the heart of Anne of Brittany.

musee-du-chateau.name: Dourdan Castle Museum
musee-du-chateau.description: Museum inside the château of Dourdan, a well-preserved fortress built around 1220 for King Philip Augustus and long used as a prison. Its collections cover the castle's history, local archaeology and medieval pottery.

musee-du-chateau-de-flers.name: Château de Flers Museum
musee-du-chateau-de-flers.description: A moated Flemish brick château, built in 1661 in the former village of Flers-Bourg and now an emblem of Villeneuve-d'Ascq. Restored by the new town, it today houses the tourist office and exhibition rooms devoted to local archaeology and history.

musee-du-chateau-des-ducs-de-wurtemberg.name: Museum of the Château des Ducs de Wurtemberg
musee-du-chateau-des-ducs-de-wurtemberg.description: The museum occupies the château of Montbéliard, residence of the principality's princes, whose origins go back to the 13th century. Born in 1843, it presents the history of the château and the principality, the former apartments of the princesses of Württemberg, and a fine art museum, along with the Georges-Cuvier archaeology and natural history collections.

musee-du-cloitre-de-notre-dame-en-vaux.name: Museum of the Cloister of Notre-Dame-en-Vaux
musee-du-cloitre-de-notre-dame-en-vaux.description: Opened in 1976, this museum of sacred art grew from the excavations conducted from 1963 by Léon Pressouyre on the chapter cloister of Notre-Dame-en-Vaux, built around 1170 and destroyed in the 1760s. It displays 77 column-statues and capitals, major witnesses to the transition from Romanesque to Gothic.

musee-du-colombier.name: Colombier Museum
musee-du-colombier.description: Set in a château built under Louis XIII by the Rocheblave family, at the heart of a farming estate that became a public park and was acquired by the city in 1951, the museum opened in 1967. It brings together local archaeology, mineralogy, decorative arts and fine art, with works by Jean Bellegambe and Jan Brueghel the Elder.

musee-du-compagnonnage.name: Tours Museum of Compagnonnage
musee-du-compagnonnage.description: Created in 1968 in the buildings of the former Saint-Julien abbey, it is the oldest and foremost museum devoted to compagnonnage, the French guild tradition. It traces the history of the compagnons and displays a great many masterpieces produced at the end of the Tour de France, across nearly every trade.

musee-du-dessin-et-de-l-estampe-original.name: Gravelines Museum of Drawing and Original Prints
musee-du-dessin-et-de-l-estampe-original.description: Created in 1982 by artists from the Nord, it is the only French museum entirely devoted to the original print. It occupies the Arsenal, a former stronghold erected by Charles V in 1528 within the fortifications, and holds 10,000 prints, from Dürer's Apocalypse to lithographs by Wifredo Lam.

musee-du-domaine-royal-de-marly-louvecie.name: Museum of the Royal Estate of Marly – Louveciennes / Marly-le-Roi
musee-du-domaine-royal-de-marly-louvecie.description: Museum devoted to the vanished royal estate of Marly, Louis XIV's retreat from Versailles. Paintings, sculptures and models evoke the demolished château, its gardens and the famous Marly machine that raised Seine water to the fountains.

musee-du-fort-de-la-pompelle.name: Fort de la Pompelle Museum
musee-du-fort-de-la-pompelle.description: A fortification in Reims' defensive ring, built from 1880 to 1883 under the Séré de Rivières system, the fort was the linchpin of the city's defence during the First World War. Now a museum, it holds weapons, uniforms and trench artefacts, as well as more than 300 German military headdresses from the former Charles Friese collection.

musee-du-gevaudan.name: Gévaudan Museum
musee-du-gevaudan.description: Successor to the first museum of Mende, opened in 1836 by the Société des Lettres, Sciences et Arts de la Lozère, it reopened in 2022 in the Hôtel de Ressouches, a 17th-century mansion. Archaeology, history and fine art there trace the past of the Gévaudan, from Gallo-Roman antiquity to the present day.

musee-du-jouet-pierre-pinel.name: Pierre Pinel Toy Museum
musee-du-jouet-pierre-pinel.description: Toy museum set in the fortified 14th-century gatehouse of Poissy's former royal priory, founded by Philip the Fair. Some 800 French toys from 1850 to 1950 include porcelain dolls, teddy bears, rocking horses and electric trains.

musee-du-louvre.name: The Louvre
musee-du-louvre.description: The world's largest art museum, housed in the former palace of the French kings. Its collections run from antiquity to 1848, from Egyptian antiquities and the Venus de Milo to the Mona Lisa, entered beneath I. M. Pei's glass pyramid.

musee-du-louvre-lens.name: Louvre-Lens
musee-du-louvre-lens.description: A satellite of the Louvre, opened in December 2012 on the site of the former Pit No. 9 of the Lens mines, in a complex of glass and aluminium pavilions designed by the Japanese firm SANAA. Its Galerie du Temps unfolds five millennia of art history in a single chronological display, whose masterpieces on loan from Paris are regularly rotated.

musee-du-masque-de-fer-et-du-fort-royal.name: Museum of the Iron Mask and Fort Royal
musee-du-masque-de-fer-et-du-fort-royal.description: Set in the Vieux Château of Fort Royal on the Île Sainte-Marguerite, built in the 17th century over Roman cisterns. Created in 1977 as the Musée de la Mer and renamed in 2020, it presents the state prisons built under Louis XIV, Roman frescoes, and the finds of land and underwater excavations.

musee-du-moyen-age-thermes-et-hotel-de-c.name: Cluny Museum – National Museum of the Middle Ages
musee-du-moyen-age-thermes-et-hotel-de-c.description: France's national museum of the Middle Ages, set in the Gallo-Roman baths of Lutetia and the 15th-century Hôtel de Cluny. Medieval sculpture, stained glass and goldwork surround the celebrated Lady and the Unicorn tapestries.

musee-du-nouveau-monde.name: New World Museum
musee-du-nouveau-monde.description: Housed since 1982 in the Hôtel Fleuriau, an 18th-century mansion built for a family of La Rochelle shipowners, the museum is devoted to relations between La Rochelle and the Americas. The first French museum to address a port's slave-trading past, it holds nearly 2,200 works related to the slave trade and the Caribbean colonies.

musee-du-noyonnais.name: Museum of the Noyonnais
musee-du-noyonnais.description: Housed in the former episcopal palace of Noyon, of which elevations dating from the 1170s and the ruins of the bishops' chapel survive. Refurbished in 1996 and restored in 2019, it presents the history of the town since Gallo-Roman times, pieces from the cathedral treasury and an 11th-century chess set.

musee-du-papier.name: Paper Museum
musee-du-papier.description: Opened in 1988 on the banks of the Charente, in the former Bardou Le Nil paper mill, which made cigarette paper until its closure in 1970. A waterwheel, pulp vats and a tall chimney bear witness to the site's activity, where the industrial papermaking of the Charente and its related industries are explored.

musee-du-parfum-fragonard.name: Fragonard Perfume Museum
musee-du-parfum-fragonard.description: Museum of the Grasse perfume house Fragonard, in a Napoleon III townhouse near the Opéra Garnier. Copper stills, essences and antique flacons trace three thousand years of perfume-making, from ancient Egypt to modern extraction techniques.

musee-du-pavillon-de-vendome.name: Pavillon de Vendôme-Dobler Museum
musee-du-pavillon-de-vendome.description: Mansion built from 1665 onward for Louis de Mercœur, Duke of Vendôme and governor of Provence, set amid a French formal garden. Restored in the early 20th century by the collector Henri Dobler, whose name it also bears, it now houses a municipal museum and exhibitions of contemporary art and photography.

musee-du-pays-de-sarrebourg.name: Museum of the Sarrebourg Area
musee-du-pays-de-sarrebourg.description: Founded in 1905 and initially devoted to archaeology, the museum has occupied a building by the architect Bernard Desmoulin since 2003. It presents more than 800 pieces tracing the history of the Sarrebourg area, earthenware and porcelain from Niderviller, and the preparatory drawings for the stained-glass windows Marc Chagall made for the nearby Chapelle des Cordeliers.

musee-du-petit-palais.name: Petit Palais Museum
musee-du-petit-palais.description: A former 14th-century cardinal's residence that became the home of the archbishops of Avignon, the Petit Palais has housed a museum of medieval and early Renaissance painting and sculpture since 1976. Its 326 Italian primitives, drawn mainly from the Campana collection, form the richest such group in France after that of the Louvre.

musee-du-quai-branly-jacques-chirac.name: Quai Branly Museum – Jacques Chirac
musee-du-quai-branly-jacques-chirac.description: Museum of the arts and civilisations of Africa, Asia, Oceania and the Americas, opened in 2006 in a Jean Nouvel building beside the Seine. Its collection of some 370,000 objects includes masks, textiles and ritual sculpture.

musee-du-service-de-sante-des-armees-du-.name: Museum of the Army Health Service at Val-de-Grâce
musee-du-service-de-sante-des-armees-du-.description: Museum of French military medicine, set in the cloister of the 17th-century royal abbey of Val-de-Grâce founded by Anne of Austria. Instruments, uniforms and field equipment trace the care of soldiers from the Ancien Régime to today.

musee-du-tabac-maison-peyrarede.name: Tobacco Museum (Maison Peyrarède)
musee-du-tabac-maison-peyrarede.description: Housed in the Maison Peyrarède, a 17th-century mansion built in the heart of old Bergerac and nicknamed Château Henri IV, where the shift from Renaissance to classicism can be read in the architecture. The museum traces three thousand years of tobacco history through pipes, boxes, graters and works of art from around the world.

musee-du-temps.name: Museum of Time
musee-du-temps.description: Housed in the Palais Granvelle, a Renaissance building erected from 1532 to 1540 for Nicolas Perrenot de Granvelle, adviser to Charles V. Opened in 2002, it brings together one of the richest clock and watch collections in Europe, from Antide Janvier's astronomical sphere to atomic clocks, and houses a thirteen-metre Foucault pendulum.

musee-du-terroir.name: Museum of Local Heritage
musee-du-terroir.description: Museum of folk arts and traditions set up in a courtyard farm in the village of Annappes. It recreates the everyday life of people in the Nord region in the early 20th century, with a period bedroom, kitchen and classroom, and the workshops of a clog-maker, a cobbler and a farrier.

musee-du-textile-et-de-la-mode.name: Cholet Textile Museum
musee-du-textile-et-de-la-mode.description: Housed in the former Rivière-Sauvageau bleaching works of 1881, a monument to the industrial architecture of the Choletais, the museum opened in 1995. It follows the processing of hemp, flax and cotton through to weaving and bleaching, and devotes considerable space to the famous red handkerchief of Cholet.

musee-du-vieil-aix-hotel-d-estienne-de-s.name: Museum of Old Aix (Hôtel d'Estienne de Saint-Jean)
musee-du-vieil-aix-hotel-d-estienne-de-s.description: Housed in the Hôtel d'Estienne de Saint-Jean, an Aix mansion of the 1670s-1680s that has kept its painted decor, plasterwork and ironwork. Opened in 1932 at the initiative of Marie d'Estienne de Saint-Jean, it evokes the history of the town from the 17th to the 19th century and displays the puppets of the talking Nativity crib and the Fête-Dieu procession.

musee-du-vieux-nimes.name: Museum of Old Nîmes
musee-du-vieux-nimes.description: Founded in 1920 by the Nîmes scholar Henry Bauquier, the museum occupies the former episcopal palace of the late 17th century, on Place aux Herbes near the cathedral. Its collections of regional ethnography evoke life in Nîmes since the Middle Ages and the textile industry, including the famous serge de Nîmes, the ancestor of denim.

musee-du-vin-de-champagne-et-d-archeolog.name: Museum of Champagne Wine and Regional Archaeology - Château Perrier
musee-du-vin-de-champagne-et-d-archeolog.description: Set up in the Château Perrier, a vast eclectic mansion built from 1852 to 1857 for Charles Nicolas Perrier by the Épernay architect Eugène Cordier, on Avenue de Champagne. Reopened in 2021 after restoration, it presents the geology, regional archaeology and history of Champagne wine.

musee-dunoyer-de-segonzac.name: Dunoyer de Segonzac Museum
musee-dunoyer-de-segonzac.description: Small municipal museum honouring painter and engraver André Dunoyer de Segonzac (1884-1974), born in Boussy-Saint-Antoine. It holds etchings, lithographs, posters, photographs and books largely from the artist's own library.

musee-dupuy-mestreau.name: Dupuy-Mestreau Museum
musee-dupuy-mestreau.description: Housed in the Hôtel Monconseil, built in 1738 for the Marquis Étienne Guinot de Monconseil on the banks of the Charente. Assembled from 1920 onward by the collector Abel Mestreau, it holds a rich collection of Saintonge folk arts and traditions, including headdresses, costumes, furniture, earthenware and reconstructed period rooms.

musee-emile-jean.name: Émile Jean Museum
musee-emile-jean.description: Local history museum founded in 1973 by the historical society of Villiers-sur-Marne, in a 19th-century house. Documents, photographs and everyday objects recreate life in the Brie region, from village school days to the war of 1870.

musee-esteve-hotel-des-echevins.name: Hôtel des Échevins
musee-esteve-hotel-des-echevins.description: Bourges town hall built from 1489 for the city's aldermen, with a main wing and a Flamboyant Gothic stair turret recalling the Palais Jacques-Cœur, and a Renaissance gallery added in 1623. Listed as a historic monument as early as 1886, it has housed the Musée Estève since 1987, devoted to the abstract painter Maurice Estève (1904-2001).

musee-eugene-boudin.name: Eugène Boudin Museum
musee-eugene-boudin.description: Founded in 1868 at the initiative of the Honfleur painter Louis-Alexandre Dubourg, the museum moved in 1924 into the chapel of the former Augustinian convent. It brings together views of the Seine estuary by Eugène Boudin, Claude Monet, Gustave Courbet and Eugène Isabey.

musee-eugene-delacroix.name: Eugène Delacroix Museum
musee-eugene-delacroix.description: The last home and studio of Romantic painter Eugène Delacroix, on the quiet place de Furstenberg, where he lived from 1857 until his death in 1863. Paintings, drawings and personal memorabilia are shown in his apartment and garden studio.

musee-fabre.name: Fabre Museum
musee-fabre.description: Born in 1828 from the donation of the Montpellier painter François-Xavier Fabre, the museum occupies the Hôtel de Massilian and former buildings of the Jesuit college. Reopened in 2007 after four years of work, it displays more than two thousand paintings, from Bonjour Monsieur Courbet to rooms devoted to Pierre Soulages.

musee-fayet.name: Béziers Museum of Fine Arts
musee-fayet.description: Founded in 1859 by the Archaeological, Scientific and Literary Society of Béziers, the Museum of Fine Arts occupies two mansions. The Hôtel Fayet, given to the city in 1966, displays 19th-century paintings and sculpture along with the studio of the Béziers sculptor Jean-Antoine Injalbert.

musee-fenaille.name: Fenaille Museum
musee-fenaille.description: Housed in the Hôtel de Jouéry, a mansion given to the city in 1929 by the patron Maurice Fenaille, the museum opened in 1937. It holds its famous collection of Rouergue statue-menhirs, alongside Gallo-Roman antiquities, medieval sculpture and six works by Rodin.

musee-flaubert-et-d-histoire-de-la-medec.name: Flaubert Museum and Museum of the History of Medicine
musee-flaubert-et-d-histoire-de-la-medec.description: Set up in 1945 in the house where Gustave Flaubert was born, within the former Hôtel-Dieu of Rouen built by Jean-Baptiste Le Brument. It combines mementoes of the writer, born here in 1821, with collections on the history of medicine, including Angélique du Coudray's childbirth mannequin, pharmacy earthenware and surgical instrument sets.

musee-fragonard.name: Fragonard Museum
musee-fragonard.description: One of France's oldest museums, created in 1766 within the Alfort veterinary school. Its anatomy and pathology collections culminate in Honoré Fragonard's 18th-century flayed figures, including his famous horseman of the Apocalypse.

musee-francais-de-la-carte-a-jouer-et-ga.name: French Playing Card Museum
musee-francais-de-la-carte-a-jouer-et-ga.description: The only museum in France devoted to playing cards, with historic decks, tarots and engraving plates from around the world. An adjoining gallery recounts the history of Issy-les-Moulineaux and its vanished château.

musee-franco-americain-du-chateau-de-ble.name: Franco-American Museum at the Château de Blérancourt
musee-franco-americain-du-chateau-de-ble.description: Château built from 1612 to 1619 by Salomon de Brosse, bought in ruins by the American philanthropist Anne Morgan, whose committee had aided the devastated regions of the Aisne during the Great War. It became a museum in 1924 and a national museum in 1931, and traces Franco-American relations since the War of Independence.

musee-francois-rude.name: François Rude Museum
musee-francois-rude.description: Housed in the north transept of the former Saint-Étienne church, founded in the 11th century and Dijon's cathedral from 1731 to 1792 before becoming a grain hall and then a commodities exchange. It displays plaster casts of works by the Dijon sculptor François Rude, including The Departure of the Volunteers of 1792 from the Arc de Triomphe.

musee-garinet.name: Garinet Museum
musee-garinet.description: House of the early 16th century in chalk and brick, residence of the bishop of Châlons's vidame until the Revolution, and later home of the bibliophile Jules Garinet. Bequeathed to the city, it became a museum in 1899 and displays paintings of the Northern, French and Italian schools, decorative arts, and ninety-eight wooden models of French monuments.

musee-goya-musee-d-art-hispanique.name: Goya Museum
musee-goya-musee-d-art-hispanique.description: Housed in the former episcopal palace built in 1675 to plans by Jules Hardouin-Mansart, surrounded by gardens laid out by Le Nôtre. It became the Musée Goya in 1947 following donations from the Briguiboul family, and holds one of the richest collections of Hispanic art in France, with works by Velázquez, Murillo and Ribera and Goya's great print series.

musee-granet.name: Granet Museum
musee-granet.description: Founded in 1828 in the former priory of the Knights of Malta, adjoining the church of Saint-Jean-de-Malte. Enriched in 1849 by the bequest of the Aix painter François-Marius Granet, it displays paintings and sculpture from the 14th to the 20th century, nine canvases by Cézanne, and, in the Chapelle des Pénitents Blancs, the Jean Planque collection.

musee-grobet-labadie-mgl.name: Musée Grobet-Labadié (MGL)
musee-grobet-labadie-mgl.description: Mansion built in 1873 by the architect Gabriel Clauzel for the industrialist Alexandre Labadié, facing the Palais Longchamp. His daughter Marie donated it to the city in 1919 along with more than seven thousand works; opened in 1926, it holds furniture, tapestries, earthenware, musical instruments and paintings in their original setting.

musee-gustave-courbet.name: Courbet Museum
musee-gustave-courbet.description: Set up in the Hôtel Hébert, a 16th-century house remodelled in the 18th century, where Gustave Courbet was born in 1819. Founded in 1947 at the initiative of the painter Robert Fernier and opened on this site in 1971, it was enlarged between 2008 and 2011 and holds paintings, drawings, sculpture and archives of the master of Ornans.

musee-gustave-moreau.name: Gustave Moreau Museum
musee-gustave-moreau.description: House and studio of Symbolist painter Gustave Moreau, arranged as a museum by the artist himself before his death in 1898. Thousands of his paintings, watercolours and drawings hang floor to ceiling around a spiral staircase.

musee-hebert.name: Hébert Museum
musee-hebert.description: Family home of the painter Ernest Hébert (1817-1908), set in a two-hectare park, where the artist stayed between his periods in Italy. Turned into a museum by his widow Gabrielle in 1934, it displays his works, his reconstructed studio, and paintings by fellow Dauphiné artists of his time.

musee-hebre.name: Musée Hèbre
musee-hebre.description: Museum of art and history founded in the second half of the 19th century, housed in the Hôtel Hèbre de Saint-Clément and renovated in 2006. Its collections combine fine art with non-European ethnology brought back by travellers from Rochefort; the ground floor holds a relief model of the town made in 1835.

musee-hector-berlioz.name: Hector Berlioz Museum
musee-hector-berlioz.description: House where Hector Berlioz was born, built in 1680 and remodelled around 1730 by his family, in the centre of La Côte-Saint-André. Opened as a museum in 1935 and renovated for the composer's bicentenary, it holds period furniture, scores, letters, instruments and an Érard piano acquired by his wife in 1847.

musee-henri-chapu.name: Henri Chapu Museum
musee-henri-chapu.description: Museum in sculptor Henri Chapu's native village, created in 1887 with works he gave to Le Mée-sur-Seine. More than sixty plaster models and bronzes trace the career of this leading official sculptor of 19th-century France.

musee-henri-martin.name: Cahors Henri-Martin Museum
musee-henri-martin.description: Housed in the former episcopal palace, built around 1470, this museum, founded in 1833, opened to the public in 1929 and reopened in May 2022 after six years of work. It holds a major group of works by the painter Henri Martin, mementoes of Léon Gambetta, a native of Cahors, and archaeological collections.

musee-historique-de-haguenau.name: Haguenau Historical Museum
musee-historique-de-haguenau.description: Neo-Gothic and neo-Renaissance building built from 1900 to 1905 by the Strasbourg architects Kuder and Müller, at the request of the mayor Xavier Nessel to house his collections. On display are Bronze and Iron Age archaeology, Gallo-Roman and Merovingian pieces, Hannong earthenware and manuscripts from the workshop of Diebold Lauber.

musee-historique-de-mulhouse.name: Mulhouse Historical Museum
musee-historique-de-mulhouse.description: Housed since 1969 in the former town hall on Place de la Réunion, a 16th-century Rhenish Renaissance building with painted façades. Founded in 1864, it displays furniture, costumes, toys, tools and reconstructed Alsatian interiors, along with the Klapperstein, the 'gossips' stone'.

musee-historique-de-strasbourg.name: Strasbourg Historical Museum
musee-historique-de-strasbourg.description: Housed in the Grande Boucherie, built from 1586 to 1588 on the banks of the Ill. Founded in 1920 and long closed, it reopened in 2007 and traces the city's history from the Middle Ages to the present day; its relief map of 1727, covering nearly eighty square metres, is its centrepiece.

musee-hotel-le-vergeur-maison-hugues-kra.name: Hôtel Le Vergeur Museum - Maison Hugues Krafft
musee-hotel-le-vergeur-maison-hugues-kra.description: House on Place du Forum, part of which dates back to the 13th century, enlarged in the 16th century by the merchant Nicolas Le Vergeur, ruined in 1914-1918 and then restored by the architect Adolphe Prost. Acquired in 1909 by the collector Hugues Krafft, it holds his bequest, including fifty engravings by Albrecht Dürer.

musee-industriel-de-la-corderie-vallois.name: Vallois Ropeworks Industrial Museum
musee-industriel-de-la-corderie-vallois.description: Former cotton mill converted into a mechanised ropeworks in 1880 by Jules Vallois, in the Cailly valley. Listed as a historic monument in 1975, it has kept its 19th-century machinery, still driven by a waterwheel during demonstrations.

musee-ingres-bourdelle.name: Ingres-Bourdelle Museum
musee-ingres-bourdelle.description: Housed in the former 17th-century episcopal palace, which became the town hall after the Revolution. Born from the donation Ingres made to his native city in 1851, it holds the largest collection of the painter's drawings in the world, some 4,500 sheets, and has devoted a floor to the sculptor Antoine Bourdelle since 2019.

musee-international-d-art-naif-anatole-j.name: Anatole Jakovsky International Museum of Naive Art
musee-international-d-art-naif-anatole-j.description: Housed in the Château Sainte-Hélène, a former property of the perfumer François Coty, in the Fabron district. Opened in 1982 around the donation of Renée and Anatole Jakovsky, it brings together hundreds of works of naive art, from Henri Rousseau (the 'Douanier') to Séraphine de Senlis and Grandma Moses.

musee-international-de-la-parfumerie-mip.name: International Museum of Perfume
musee-international-de-la-parfumerie-mip.description: Heir to the museum founded in 1918 by François Carnot, it was inaugurated in its present form in 1989 around the Hôtel de Pontevès, a mansion of 1778, and a stretch of medieval ramparts. Its roughly fifty thousand objects trace the history of perfume from antiquity to the present day, including raw materials, stills, bottles, posters and toiletry items.

musee-jardin-paul-landowski.name: Paul Landowski Garden Museum
musee-jardin-paul-landowski.description: Garden museum on the site of the Boulogne studio of Paul Landowski, sculptor of Rio de Janeiro's Christ the Redeemer. Around a hundred sculptures and models are displayed in the garden and two underground galleries.

musee-jean-aicard-paulin-bertrand-mab.name: Musée Jean Aicard – Paulin Bertrand (MAB)
musee-jean-aicard-paulin-bertrand-mab.description: Les Lauriers Roses, a Provençal villa set in a six-hectare park laid out by the writer Jean Aicard, author of Maurin des Maures, who lived there until his death. Bequeathed to Toulon in 1960 by the widow of the painter Paulin Bertrand, Aicard's heir, it holds mementoes of both men, the painter's studio, and ceramics by Clément Massier.

musee-jean-calvin.name: Jean Calvin Museum
musee-jean-calvin.description: Museum devoted to the reformer Jean Calvin (1509-1564), born in Noyon, and to the history of the Reformation. Built on Place Aristide-Briand, on the site of his birthplace, it holds 16th- and 17th-century bibles, books and documents relating to Protestantism.

musee-jean-claude-boulard-carre-plantage.name: Jean-Claude-Boulard Museum — Carré Plantagenêt
musee-jean-claude-boulard-carre-plantage.description: Museum of the archaeology and history of Le Mans, opened in 2009 in the Saint-Nicolas district to designs by the architect Bernard Althabegoïty. Its displays run from prehistory to medieval Maine and include the Plantagenet enamel plaque, the Sablons treasure, the Coëffort treasure and six recumbent effigies.

musee-jean-cocteau-le-bastion.name: Jean Cocteau Museum - Le Bastion
musee-jean-cocteau-le-bastion.description: A 17th-century bastion that guarded Menton's old harbour, noticed by Jean Cocteau in 1957, who converted it into a museum himself: the pebble mosaics, display cases and decor are his own work. Opened in 1966, after the poet's death, it shows drawings, ceramics, tapestries and pastels on a rotating basis.

musee-jean-jacques-henner.name: Jean-Jacques Henner Museum
musee-jean-jacques-henner.description: National museum devoted to Alsatian painter Jean-Jacques Henner (1829-1905), in a Plaine Monceau townhouse that belonged to fellow painter Guillaume Dubufe. It displays Henner's portraits, landscapes and idealised nudes.

musee-jean-jacques-rousseau.name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau Museum
musee-jean-jacques-rousseau.description: The modest Mont-Louis house in Montmorency where Jean-Jacques Rousseau lived from 1757 to 1762 and wrote Julie, Émile and The Social Contract. Period rooms and the garden pavilion evoke the philosopher's daily life.

musee-jean-leon-gerome.name: Jean-Léon Gérôme Museum
musee-jean-leon-gerome.description: Founded in 1882 at the initiative of the painter Victor Jeanneney, the museum occupies the former Ursuline convent built from 1680 to 1683. It holds Gallo-Roman funerary stelae and the largest group of works by Jean-Léon Gérôme, a native of Vesoul, whose name it took in 2024.

musee-jean-lurcat-et-de-la-tapisserie-co.name: Jean Lurçat and Contemporary Tapestry Museum
musee-jean-lurcat-et-de-la-tapisserie-co.description: Housed in the former Hôpital Saint-Jean, founded in the late 12th century, whose patients' hall with its Angevin vaulting has held Le Chant du monde since 1968, a suite of ten tapestries woven by Jean Lurçat from 1957 to 1966. The museum also presents contemporary textile art, with works by Thomas Gleb and Josep Grau-Garriga.

musee-joseph-dechelette.name: Joseph Déchelette Museum of Fine Arts and Archaeology
musee-joseph-dechelette.description: Roanne's municipal museum, opened in 1844 thanks to the archaeologist Fleury Mulsant, it bears the name of Joseph Déchelette, curator from 1892 and a major figure in archaeology, who bequeathed it his collections. It has occupied his family's mansion since 1923 and displays regional archaeology, fine art and earthenware.

musee-jules-verne.name: Jules Verne Museum
musee-jules-verne.description: Bourgeois house built from 1872 to 1878 by the architect Ernest-Marie Buron on the Butte Sainte-Anne, overlooking the Loire and the harbour. Opened in 1978 for the 150th anniversary of the Nantes-born writer's birth, it brings together editions, manuscripts, posters, illustrations and personal objects given by his descendants.

musee-lambinet.name: Lambinet Museum
musee-lambinet.description: Versailles's municipal museum, set in an elegant 18th-century townhouse, with period interiors, fine and decorative arts, and collections on the city's history, notably the French Revolution.

musee-laperouse.name: Lapérouse Museum
musee-laperouse.description: Founded in 1988 by the city of Albi and the Lapérouse Albi-France association, the museum occupies the restored old Albi mills, with their red-brick vaults. It brings together some 640 objects relating to the Albi-born navigator Jean-François de Lapérouse, including models, instruments, family mementoes and remains from La Boussole and L'Astrolabe.

musee-lapidaire-avignon.name: Lapidary Museum
musee-lapidaire-avignon.description: Housed in the baroque chapel of the Jesuit college, built from 1620 to 1655 by Étienne Martellange and François de Royers de la Valfenière. Descended from the cabinet of the collector Esprit Calvet, it displays Greek, Roman and Gallo-Roman sculpture, including the Tarasque of Noves and the Warrior of Mondragon.

musee-le-secq-des-tournelles.name: Le Secq des Tournelles Museum
musee-le-secq-des-tournelles.description: Housed in the former church of Saint-Laurent, a Flamboyant Gothic building of the 15th and 16th centuries. Founded in 1920 thanks to the gift of Henri Le Secq des Tournelles, it holds the largest collection of antique ironwork displayed in any museum: more than fifteen thousand signs, locks, door knockers, keys and iron jewellery.

musee-leblanc-duvernoy.name: Leblanc-Duvernoy Museum
musee-leblanc-duvernoy.description: An 18th-century mansion bequeathed to the city in 1926 by the music-lover Paul Leblanc-Duvernoy. It holds Nivernais earthenware and Puisaye stoneware, revolutionary and monogrammed earthenware, and a Beauvais tapestry hanging depicting the history of the Emperor of China, in the music room.

musee-librairie-du-compagnonnage.name: Compagnonnage Museum and Bookshop
musee-librairie-du-compagnonnage.description: Small museum of the compagnons du Tour de France craft guilds, displaying masterpieces made by journeymen — model staircases and works in wood, stone and iron — alongside a bookshop devoted to the guild tradition.

musee-magnelli-musee-de-la-ceramique.name: Magnelli Museum, Ceramics Museum
musee-magnelli-musee-de-la-ceramique.description: Former 16th-century priory of the monks of Lérins, lords of Vallauris, of which a medieval chapel and a Renaissance staircase survive. Opened in 1977, it brings together the work of the abstract painter Alberto Magnelli, donated by his widow, and an overview of local ceramics, from the Massier family to pieces produced by Picasso at the Madoura workshop.

musee-mandet.name: Mandet Museum
musee-mandet.description: Founded in 1866 by Francisque Mandet, the museum occupies the Hôtel Dufraisse du Cheix, a Louis XV-style mansion built in Volvic stone from 1707 onward. Fine art, Mediterranean archaeology and decorative arts sit alongside the 5,500 works given in 1983 by Monsieur and Madame Richard.

musee-maritime-de-la-rochelle.name: La Rochelle Maritime Museum
musee-maritime-de-la-rochelle.description: A floating museum opened in 1988 in the trawler basin of the Vieux-Port, it preserves nine vessels, eight of them listed as historic monuments. Visitors can tour the weather ship France 1, launched in 1958, the trawler Angoumois and Bernard Moitessier's ketch Joshua.

musee-massena.name: Masséna Museum
musee-massena.description: A holiday villa built from 1898 to 1901 by Hans-Georg Tersling and Aaron Messiah for Victor Masséna, Prince of Essling, in an Italian neoclassical style tinged with Empire. Given to the city in 1919, it has housed a museum of the history of Nice since 1921, which includes Gros's Portrait of the Empress Joséphine.

musee-massey-musee-international-des-hus.name: Massey Museum — International Museum of the Hussars
musee-massey-musee-international-des-hus.description: A building in an Oriental-inspired style topped by a belvedere tower, designed by the architect Jean-Jacques Latour for the botanist Placide Massey, who bequeathed his garden and this unfinished building to Tarbes on his death in 1853. It houses the International Museum of the Hussars, more than 15,000 pieces covering four centuries and some thirty countries.

musee-matisse.name: Matisse Museum
musee-matisse.description: Housed in the Villa des Arènes, a Genoese-inspired mansion built from 1670 to 1685 on the Cimiez hill, the museum opened in 1963. It traces the entire career of Henri Matisse, who lived in Nice from 1917 to 1954, through paintings, cut-outs, drawings, sculptures and illustrated books.

musee-memorial-de-la-bataille-de-normand.name: Memorial Museum of the Battle of Normandy
musee-memorial-de-la-bataille-de-normand.description: Opened on 14 July 1981 in Bayeux, the first major town liberated after D-Day, it recounts the seventy-seven days of the Battle of Normandy, from 7 June to 29 August 1944. Uniforms, weapons and military vehicles, including Sherman and Churchill Crocodile tanks, accompany a documentary film.

musee-municipal.name: Moret-sur-Loing Municipal Museum
musee-municipal.description: Local history museum of Moret-sur-Loing, the fortified medieval town on the Loing where Alfred Sisley spent his final years; its collection of over 1,400 objects retraces the town's past and notable figures.

musee-municipal-91150.name: Étampes Intercommunal Museum
musee-municipal-91150.description: Founded in 1875 beside the town hall, this museum covers the Étampes region from fossils and medieval archaeology to 19th-century works by local artists such as sculptor Élias Robert and painter Narcisse Berchère.

musee-municipal-d-art-et-d-histoire.name: Colombes Municipal Museum of Art and History
musee-municipal-d-art-et-d-histoire.description: Municipal museum tracing the history of Colombes, from Gallo-Roman archaeology and the 17th-century estate of Henrietta of England to local industries such as Hispano-Suiza and the Olympic stadium of the 1924 Games.

musee-municipal-ducastel-vera-de-saint-g.name: Ducastel-Vera Municipal Museum of Saint-Germain-en-Laye
musee-municipal-ducastel-vera-de-saint-g.description: Saint-Germain-en-Laye's municipal collection, born of Louis-Alexandre Ducastel's 1872 bequest: nearly 9,000 works from Egyptian antiquity to the 20th century, including fine 18th-century pastels and a preserved royal apothecary.

musee-municipal-robert-dubois-corneau.name: Robert Dubois-Corneau Municipal Museum
musee-municipal-robert-dubois-corneau.description: Housed in the former home of collector Robert Dubois-Corneau, this museum tells the story of Brunoy and the Yerres valley through paintings, prints and objets d'art from the 18th century to the present day.

musee-museum-departemental-des-hautes-al.name: Hautes-Alpes Departmental Museum
musee-museum-departemental-des-hautes-al.description: Opened to the public in September 1910 in a building erected from 1903 to 1910 to plans by the architect Chaudier, it brings together archaeology, fine art, ethnography and natural history. On display are the marble mausoleum of the Duke of Lesdiguières, carved by Jacob Richier, and a Bronze Age belt discovered at Réallon.

musee-narbo-via.name: Narbo Via
musee-narbo-via.description: Archaeology museum opened in 2021 in a building designed by the Foster + Partners agency. It presents the Roman collections of Narbonne, capital of the province of Gallia Narbonensis, around a vast wall of carved stone, and belongs to the institution that also manages Amphoralis and the Horreum.

musee-national-adrien-dubouche.name: National Adrien Dubouché Museum
musee-national-adrien-dubouche.description: Founded in 1845, this national museum owes its name to Adrien Dubouché, who directed it from 1865 and enriched it with his gifts. Its 1900 building, by Pierre-Henri Mayeux, houses some 18,000 pieces of ceramics and glass, including the largest public collection of Limoges porcelain.

musee-national-de-l-histoire-et-des-cult.name: National Museum of the History of Immigration
musee-national-de-l-histoire-et-des-cult.description: France's national museum of immigration history, housed in the Art Deco Palais de la Porte Dorée built for the 1931 Colonial Exhibition; collections and personal testimonies trace two centuries of migration to France.

musee-national-de-la-legion-d-honneur-et.name: National Museum of the Legion of Honour and Orders of Chivalry
musee-national-de-la-legion-d-honneur-et.description: Set in the Hôtel de Salm opposite the Musée d'Orsay, this museum displays decorations, insignia and paintings tracing the Legion of Honour, founded by Napoleon in 1802, and orders of chivalry from France and abroad.

musee-national-de-la-maison-bonaparte.name: Maison Bonaparte Museum
musee-national-de-la-maison-bonaparte.description: The Bonaparte family home in Ajaccio, where Napoleon was born on 15 August 1769 and spent his childhood. Now a national museum, it displays family furniture, portraits and mementoes, and evokes the history of the house and Corsican society as much as the emperor's career.

musee-national-de-la-marine.name: National Maritime Museum
musee-national-de-la-marine.description: One of the world's oldest maritime museums, at the Palais de Chaillot, tracing French naval history through ship models, paintings, figureheads and instruments, from the age of sail to modern seafaring.

musee-national-de-la-marine-brest.name: National Maritime Museum, Brest
musee-national-de-la-marine-brest.description: Set in the Château de Brest, a fortress of Roman origin commanding the mouth of the Penfeld and listed as a historic monument in 1923. Its rooms trace the history of the arsenal and the navy through ship models, sculptures by Yves Collet, navigational instruments and a German Seehund-class submarine.

musee-national-de-la-marine-port-louis-c.name: National Maritime Museum, Port-Louis
musee-national-de-la-marine-port-louis-c.description: Housed in the citadel of Port-Louis, a fortification commanding the entrance to the Lorient roadstead, the museum opened there in 1962 before being entirely redesigned. It now presents the history of sea rescue and the trade routes to the Far East, with porcelain recovered from shipwrecks.

musee-national-de-la-marine-rochefort-an.name: Rochefort School of Naval Medicine
musee-national-de-la-marine-rochefort-an.description: The world's first school of naval surgery, founded in 1722 in Rochefort and housed from 1788 in a pavilion of the naval hospital. A branch of the National Maritime Museum, it has kept its old library, anatomy amphitheatre and cabinets of natural history collections intact.

musee-national-de-la-marine-rochefort-ho.name: National Maritime Museum, Rochefort
musee-national-de-la-marine-rochefort-ho.description: The museum occupies the Hôtel de Cheusses, an early 17th-century mansion that became the headquarters of the naval command and then of the naval stores administration after the arsenal was founded in 1666. Established in 1930 as the naval museum, it holds ship models, ornamental sculpture and navigational instruments.

musee-national-de-prehistoire.name: National Museum of Prehistory
musee-national-de-prehistoire.description: Founded in 1918 by the prehistorian Denis Peyrony in the former Château de Tayac, set against the Les Eyzies cliff, and opened in 1923. Enlarged in 2004 by the architect Jean-Pierre Buffi, it holds nearly six million objects, one of the most important Palaeolithic collections in the world.

musee-national-des-chateaux-de-malmaison.name: National Museum of the Châteaux of Malmaison and Bois-Préau
musee-national-des-chateaux-de-malmaison.description: The country residence of Napoleon and Empress Joséphine, who lived at Malmaison until her death in 1814; the château preserves its Consulate-era interiors, imperial furnishings and personal mementoes, set in a rose-filled park.

musee-national-des-chateaux-de-versaille.name: Palace of Versailles
musee-national-des-chateaux-de-versaille.description: The vast royal palace of Louis XIV and his successors, a UNESCO World Heritage site, with the Hall of Mirrors, the State Apartments, the Trianon palaces and formal gardens designed by Le Nôtre.

musee-national-des-douanes.name: National Customs Museum
musee-national-des-douanes.description: Founded in 1984 in the Hôtel des Fermes du Roi, built on Place de la Bourse between 1735 and 1738 to plans by Jacques Gabriel and decorated with sculpture by Jacques Verberckt. Its roughly 13,500 objects, uniforms, weapons, paintings and seized goods trace the history of the French customs service.

musee-national-du-chateau-de-fontaineble.name: Palace of Fontainebleau
musee-national-du-chateau-de-fontaineble.description: A residence of French sovereigns for eight centuries, from the Capetians to Napoleon III; the palace preserves exceptional Renaissance interiors created for François I, Napoleon's apartments and extensive gardens, a UNESCO World Heritage site.

musee-national-du-sport.name: National Sports Museum
musee-national-du-sport.description: Founded in 1963 by Jean Durry, this national museum traces the history of sport from its origins through more than 45,000 objects and 400,000 documents, including jerseys, trophies, medals, posters, paintings and archives. Based in Paris for many years, it has been housed in the Allianz Riviera stadium in Nice since 2014.

musee-national-et-domaine-du-chateau-de-.name: National Museum and Estate of the Château de Pau
musee-national-et-domaine-du-chateau-de-.description: Fortress of the viscounts of Béarn remodelled by Gaston Fébus in the 14th century and then embellished during the Renaissance by Henri d'Albret and Marguerite d'Angoulême, it witnessed the birth of Henri IV in 1553. Restored under Louis-Philippe and then Napoleon III, it has been a national museum since 1927 and holds a rich collection of tapestries.

musee-national-fernand-leger.name: National Fernand Léger Museum
musee-national-fernand-leger.description: Built by the architect Andreï Svetchine on land acquired by Fernand Léger shortly before his death, the museum opened on 13 May 1960 at the initiative of Nadia Léger and Georges Bauquier. Its façade bears a vast mosaic after a cartoon by the painter; given to the state in 1967, it holds around 400 works.

musee-national-magnin.name: Magnin Museum
musee-national-magnin.description: Housed in the Hôtel Lantin, a mansion built in 1663-1664 near the Palace of the Dukes of Burgundy, the museum holds the collection assembled between 1881 and 1935 by Maurice Magnin and his sister Jeanne, bequeathed to the state in 1939. French, Italian and Northern European paintings are displayed in the setting of a collector's cabinet.

musee-national-marc-chagall.name: Marc Chagall Museum
musee-national-marc-chagall.description: National museum conceived during Marc Chagall's lifetime around the seventeen canvases of the Biblical Message, which he gave to France in 1966. Opened in 1973 in a spare building by André Hermant, it also displays stained glass, mosaic, sculpture and gouaches, one of the largest collections of the painter's work.

musee-national-pablo-picasso-la-guerre-e.name: Picasso Museum
musee-national-pablo-picasso-la-guerre-e.description: Housed in the Romanesque chapel of the former Vallauris priory, it holds War and Peace, a vast decorative scheme painted by Picasso in 1952 and displayed there since 1959. The artist had wanted a dimly lit space, to be discovered by visitors candle in hand.

musee-nicephore-niepce.name: Nicéphore Niépce Museum
musee-nicephore-niepce.description: Opened in 1974 in the former Hôtel des Messageries Royales, on the banks of the Saône, in the birthplace of Nicéphore Niépce (1765-1833), the inventor of photography. Its collections bring together nearly four million images and more than 1,500 cameras, including the very first in history.

musee-nissim-de-camondo-union-centrale-d.name: Nissim de Camondo Museum
musee-nissim-de-camondo-union-centrale-d.description: The mansion of Count Moïse de Camondo, built in 1911–1914 and kept as he left it, houses his outstanding collection of 18th-century French furniture and decorative arts; it is named for his son Nissim, killed in World War I.

musee-paul-valery.name: Paul Valéry Museum
musee-paul-valery.description: A concrete and glass building designed by Guy Guillaume and opened in November 1970 on the flank of Mont Saint-Clair, above the seaside cemetery where Paul Valéry is buried. It holds the poet's manuscripts and drawings, paintings from the 19th to the 21st century, and a collection devoted to water jousting.

musee-peynet-et-du-dessin-humoristique.name: Peynet and Cartoon Museum
musee-peynet-et-du-dessin-humoristique.description: Opened in 1989 on Place Nationale, in the town where Raymond Peynet had settled in 1976, from a donation of around three hundred works by the cartoonist. Broadened to humorous drawing after his death in 1999, it brings together some six hundred pieces, including press cartoons, posters, lithographs, dolls and ceramics.

musee-picasso.name: Picasso Museum
musee-picasso.description: The world's largest public collection of Picasso's work — paintings, sculptures, drawings and the artist's personal archives — displayed in the Hôtel Salé, a grand 17th-century mansion in the Marais.

musee-picasso-chateau-grimaldi.name: Picasso Museum (Château Grimaldi)
musee-picasso-chateau-grimaldi.description: Château built in the 15th century by the Grimaldi family on the ancient foundations of the acropolis of Antipolis, bought back by the city in 1925. Picasso set up his studio here in 1946 and left his works on deposit; it became the Musée Picasso in 1966 and holds around 245 of them, alongside works by Nicolas de Staël and Hans Hartung.

musee-pierre-corneille-maison-natale.name: Pierre Corneille Museum (Birthplace)
musee-pierre-corneille-maison-natale.description: Birthplace of Pierre Corneille, born on 6 June 1606 on Rue de la Pie, where the playwright lived for fifty-six years. Opened in 1920 and inaugurated the following year after restoration led by the architect Georges Ruel, the museum displays first editions, engravings and documents given in 1917 by the bibliophile Édouard Mélite.

musee-pierre-noel.name: Pierre Noël Museum
musee-pierre-noel.description: Opened in March 1977 in a building by the architect Aldo Travaglini that incorporates the colonnade of the former episcopal palace of 1782, it bears the name of a mayor of the town. Its collections bring together Gallo-Roman archaeology, modern art, ornithology, Vosges ethnography and mementoes of Jules Ferry.

musee-pince.name: Pincé Museum
musee-pince.description: Renaissance mansion built from 1528 to 1535 by Jean Delespine for Jean de Pincé, mayor of Angers, and given to the city in 1861 by the painter Guillaume Bodinier. A museum since 1889 and reopened in 2020, it is devoted to Mediterranean antiquities and the arts of China and Japan.

musee-pissarro.name: Pissarro-Pontoise Museum of Art and History (MAHPP)
musee-pissarro.description: Museum on the heights of Pontoise devoted to Camille Pissarro, who painted the town for nearly two decades; it holds prints and drawings by the Impressionist master along with works by painters of the Oise valley.

musee-quesnel-moriniere.name: Quesnel-Morinière Museum
musee-quesnel-moriniere.description: A 17th-century mansion next to the cathedral and the botanical garden, bequeathed to the city by Monsieur and Madame Quesnel-Morinière, its former owners; the museum was founded there in 1868 and opened in 1874. Its roughly 5,000 pieces bring together Norman paintings, religious sculpture, archaeology and Cotentin ceramics.

musee-rambolitrain.name: Rambolitrain Museum
musee-rambolitrain.description: Museum of toy and model trains in Rambouillet, with more than 4,000 pieces from the 19th century onward and a large working miniature railway that retraces the history of rail travel.

musee-regional-d-auvergne.name: Riom Museum of Folk Arts and Traditions
musee-regional-d-auvergne.description: Museum of ethnography set in a Riom house of the 15th-18th centuries, listed as a historic monument in 1928. Its roughly 4,000 objects, gathered with the help of the ethnologist Georges Henri Rivière, document life in Auvergne, particularly the region's agriculture, winegrowing and traditional trades.

musee-rodin.name: Rodin Museum
musee-rodin.description: Museum devoted to sculptor Auguste Rodin in the 18th-century Hôtel Biron, where he lived and worked; The Thinker, The Kiss and The Gates of Hell are shown in the mansion and its large sculpture garden.

musee-rodin-meudon.name: Rodin Museum, Meudon
musee-rodin-meudon.description: The Villa des Brillants in Meudon was Rodin's home and main studio; plaster casts and studies reveal the sculptor's working process, and his tomb in the garden is crowned by a cast of The Thinker.

musee-roybet-fould.name: Roybet-Fould Museum
musee-roybet-fould.description: Courbevoie's municipal museum, set in the wooden Sweden and Norway pavilion built for the 1878 World's Fair and re-erected in Bécon park. It keeps 19th-century paintings by Ferdinand Roybet and Consuelo Fould, along with works by the sculptor Jean-Baptiste Carpeaux.

musee-saint-loup.name: Musée Saint-Loup
musee-saint-loup.description: Housed since 1830 in the former Abbaye Saint-Loup, rebuilt in the 17th and 18th centuries, the museum brings together archaeology, sculpture, decorative arts and natural history. Its picture gallery, formed from revolutionary seizures and the La Chapelle-Godefroy collection, includes works by Watteau, Boucher and Hubert Robert.

musee-saint-raymond-musee-d-archeologie-.name: Musée Saint-Raymond, Toulouse Museum of Archaeology
musee-saint-raymond-musee-d-archeologie-.description: Toulouse's museum of archaeology, housed in the former Collège Saint-Raymond, built in 1523 and restored by Viollet-le-Duc from 1868 to 1871. Opened in 1892, it holds France's second-largest collection of Roman portraits, coming mainly from the Villa de Chiragan, along with a paleo-Christian necropolis visible in situ.

musee-saint-remi.name: Musée Saint-Remi
musee-saint-remi.description: Housed in the former royal Benedictine Abbaye Saint-Remi, keeper of the Holy Ampulla used in royal coronations and a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1991, the museum was founded in 1978. It presents regional archaeology, ten 16th-century tapestries depicting the life of Saint Remigius, and a substantial military section.

musee-sainte-croix.name: Musée Sainte-Croix
musee-sainte-croix.description: Opened on 21 December 1974 on the site of the former Abbaye Sainte-Croix, in a vast concrete and glass building by Jean Monge, recognised as a notable work of contemporary architecture. Its collections range from prehistory to contemporary art, including the Minerva of Poitiers and seven works by Camille Claudel.

musee-savoisien.name: Savoy Museum
musee-savoisien.description: Housed in a former 13th-century Franciscan convent, listed as a historic monument in 1911, the museum was opened on 18 November 1913. Reopened in 2023 after lengthy restoration, it holds some 70,000 pieces, including the 13th-century secular wall paintings from the Château de Cruet.

musee-soulages.name: Soulages Museum
musee-soulages.description: Opened on 30 May 2014 in the birthplace of Pierre Soulages, it occupies a building of five weathering-steel volumes designed by the Catalan agency RCR Arquitectes. It holds around five hundred works given by the artist and his wife Colette, including the cartoons for the stained-glass windows of the Conques abbey church.

musee-stendhal-appartement-gagnon.name: Stendhal Museum - Gagnon Apartment
musee-stendhal-appartement-gagnon.description: Apartment of Dr Henri Gagnon, Stendhal's maternal grandfather, at 20 Grande Rue, where the writer spent part of his childhood and discovered the family library. Together with his birthplace apartment, it forms one of the two sites of the Musée Stendhal, which displays manuscripts, early editions and documents there.

musee-thomas-henry.name: Thomas Henry Museum
musee-thomas-henry.description: Born from gifts made between 1831 and 1835 by Thomas Henry, a picture dealer and expert to the royal museums, it opened in 1835 with 163 paintings. Housed since 1983 in the Le Quasar cultural centre, it holds Italian primitives and France's second-largest collection of works by Jean-François Millet.

musee-tomi-ungerer-centre-international-.name: Tomi Ungerer Museum – International Centre for Illustration
musee-tomi-ungerer-centre-international-.description: Opened on 2 November 2007 in the Villa Greiner, built in 1884 near Place Broglie, it holds the roughly 14,000 pieces given by Tomi Ungerer (1931-2019) from 1975 onward. Children's book drawings, advertising posters, satirical works and 1,600 antique toys are shown in rotation.

musee-toulouse-lautrec.name: Toulouse-Lautrec Museum
musee-toulouse-lautrec.description: The Palais de la Berbie, a 13th-century fortress that was the residence of the bishops of Albi until 1905, has housed the museum founded through the bequest of the artist's mother since 1922. More than a thousand paintings, drawings, lithographs and posters make it the most complete collection in the world of works by Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec.

musee-victor-aubert.name: Victor Aubert Museum
musee-victor-aubert.description: A small local-history museum housed in the remains of an 11th-century Benedictine priory beside Maule's church. Founded by self-taught archaeologist Victor Aubert, it displays fossils, prehistoric and Merovingian finds, and the rural folk traditions of the area.

musee-vivant-denon.name: Musée Denon
musee-vivant-denon.description: Opened in 1866 in a former neoclassical drawing school, this museum has borne the name of Dominique Vivant Denon, a native of the region and the Louvre's first director, since 1908. It combines French, Italian and Flemish paintings from the 16th to the 19th century with rich archaeological collections recovered from the Saône.

musee-wurth-france-erstein.name: Würth Museum, Erstein
musee-wurth-france-erstein.description: Opened on 27 January 2008 near the French headquarters of the Würth group, it is the thirteenth museum founded by the industrialist and collector Reinhold Würth. It presents, in rotation, modern and contemporary works from the Würth collection, which numbers more than 16,000 pieces, from Picasso to Gerhard Richter.

musee-yves-saint-laurent-paris.name: Yves Saint Laurent Museum, Paris
