musee-yves-saint-laurent-paris.description: The historic couture house at 5 avenue Marceau where Yves Saint Laurent created his collections from 1974 to 2002, now a museum devoted to his work, holding haute couture garments, sketches and the designer's studio preserved as it was.

musee-zadkine.name: Zadkine Museum
musee-zadkine.description: The house and studios near the Luxembourg Gardens where Russian-born sculptor Ossip Zadkine lived and worked from 1928 to 1967. This City of Paris museum shows his carvings and bronzes in the workshops and a small sculpture garden.

musee-ziem.name: Ziem Museum
musee-ziem.description: Founded in 1908 following a donation from the painter Félix Ziem (1821-1911) to his adopted city, it has been housed since 1982 in a converted former customs barracks. Ziem's Venetian and Mediterranean landscapes are joined by the Marseille school, Dufy, Derain, votive paintings and local archaeology.

musee-zola-dreyfus.name: Zola-Dreyfus Museum
musee-zola-dreyfus.description: Émile Zola's country house in Médan, where he wrote much of the Rougon-Macquart cycle, paired with the first museum devoted to the Dreyfus Affair, recalling the writer's "J'accuse...!" and his fight for the captain's rehabilitation.

musee-zoologique.name: Zoological Museum
musee-zoologique.description: Heir to the cabinet of natural history assembled in the 18th century by the naturalist Jean Hermann, it is jointly run by the city and the University of Strasbourg. Reopened in September 2025 after six years of renovation, it displays, among other things, the Blaschka glass models, a coelacanth and an Atlas lion.

musees-de-sens.name: Sens Museum
musees-de-sens.description: Founded in 1844, the museum has been housed since 1985 in the former archbishops' palace, adjoining Saint-Étienne Cathedral. It holds the cathedral treasury, including the 12th-century ivory Sainte Châsse reliquary, important Gallo-Roman collections and the Villethierry hoard, comprising more than eight hundred pieces of jewellery.

musees-gadagne.name: Musées Gadagne
musees-gadagne.description: A vast mansion in Vieux-Lyon rebuilt in the 16th century and bought in 1545 by the Gadagne family, Florentine bankers whose wealth became proverbial; it was listed as a historic monument in 1920. The mansion brings together the Lyon History Museum, opened in 1921, and the Museum of Puppetry Arts, founded in 1950 around the character of Guignol.

museon-arlaten-musee-de-provence.name: Museon Arlaten
museon-arlaten-musee-de-provence.description: Museum of Provençal ethnography founded in 1896 by Frédéric Mistral, who installed it in 1904 in the Hôtel de Laval-Castellane, a former Jesuit college, using the money from his Nobel Prize in Literature. Reopened in 2021 after more than ten years of work, it displays the costumes, furniture and everyday objects of the Arles region.

museum-aquarium-de-nancy.name: Nancy Museum-Aquarium
museum-aquarium-de-nancy.description: A natural history museum descended from the cabinet of the Collège Royal de Médecine, created in 1752 by Stanislas Leszczynski, now run by the Grand Nancy metropolitan authority and the University of Lorraine. Its windowless 1933 building, by the brothers Jacques and Michel André, houses aquariums and a zoology gallery.

museum-d-histoire-naturelle-de-blois.name: Blois Natural History Museum
museum-d-histoire-naturelle-de-blois.description: Founded in the late 19th century by the Natural History Society of Loir-et-Cher, the museum has been housed since 1983 in the former Couvent des Jacobins, whose buildings date back to the 13th century. Its collections of animals, fossils, herbarium specimens and minerals shed light on the Blaisois, a crossroads of natural regions.

museum-d-histoire-naturelle-de-la-rochel.name: La Rochelle Natural History Museum
museum-d-histoire-naturelle-de-la-rochel.description: Natural history museum housed in the former residence of the governor of Aunis, built from 1708 to 1718 to plans by the royal engineer Claude Masse. Born from the cabinet given by Clément de la Faille in 1782, then enriched by the Fleuriau de Bellevue bequest in 1852, it reopened in 2007 with galleries of natural history and ethnography.

museum-d-histoire-naturelle-de-marseille.name: Marseille Natural History Museum
museum-d-histoire-naturelle-de-marseille.description: Museum founded in 1819 at the initiative of the mayor, the Marquis de Montgrand, and the prefect de Villeneuve-Bargemon. It has occupied the right wing of the Palais Longchamp, built by the architect Henri-Jacques Espérandieu, since 1869, where it displays its zoology, palaeontology and botany collections.

museum-d-histoire-naturelle-de-nantes-fe.name: Nantes Natural History Museum (closed for renovation until 2029)
museum-d-histoire-naturelle-de-nantes-fe.description: Museum born from the natural history cabinet of the pharmacist François-René Dubuisson, bought by the city in 1806 and opened in 1810. It has occupied a building erected for it on Place de la Monnaie by the architect Gustave Bourgerel since 1875, one of the first in France designed specifically for a natural history museum. It is closed for renovation until 2029.

museum-d-histoire-naturelle-de-nice.name: Nice Natural History Museum
museum-d-histoire-naturelle-de-nice.description: The oldest municipal museum in Nice, opened in 1846 around the collections of the naturalist Jean-Baptiste Vérany, joined as early as 1863 by those of Jean-Baptiste Barla, who bequeathed his buildings and holdings to the city in 1896. It holds more than a million specimens, mostly Mediterranean in origin.

museum-d-histoire-naturelle-de-rouen.name: Rouen Natural History Museum
museum-d-histoire-naturelle-de-rouen.description: Museum founded in 1828 by the mayor Adrien de Martainville and housed in the former 17th-century Couvent Sainte-Marie, with the naturalist Félix-Archimède Pouchet as its first curator. Closed to the public for ten years, it reopened in 2007 and holds more than 500,000 objects and specimens from around the world.

museum-d-histoire-naturelle-de-tours.name: Tours Natural History Museum
museum-d-histoire-naturelle-de-tours.description: The first natural history museum in Tours, opened to the public in 1853, was destroyed in the bombing of 1940; the new establishment opened on Rue du Président-Merville in 1989. It brings together a hall of natural history collections, a vivarium, a space for temporary exhibitions and a library.

museum-d-histoire-naturelle-du-havre.name: Le Havre Natural History Museum
museum-d-histoire-naturelle-du-havre.description: Museum housed since 1846 in the former law courts building of 1760, whose south wing was destroyed by the bombing of 1944. Assembled by the naturalist and draughtsman Charles-Alexandre Lesueur, its collections combine palaeontology, prehistory and zoology with 8,000 drawings and manuscripts.

museum-d-histoire-naturelle-et-de-la-pre.name: Nîmes Natural History Museum
museum-d-histoire-naturelle-et-de-la-pre.description: Museum opened in 1895 at the initiative of the Society for the Study of the Natural Sciences of Nîmes and the Gard, set around a cloister and a listed 17th-century chapel. Its galleries cover local prehistory, geology, zoology and ethnography, the last still shown in its 1930s display.

museum-d-histoire-naturelle-victor-brun.name: Victor Brun Natural History Museum
museum-d-histoire-naturelle-victor-brun.description: Founded by municipal decree in 1852 from the collections of the Montauban science society, it bears the name of the naturalist and prehistorian Victor Brun (1805-1881), its curator from 1857. Housed in the former Cour des Aides, it holds mounted birds and mammals, regional fossils and the Orgueil meteorite.

museum-de-bordeaux-sciences-et-nature.name: Muséum de Bordeaux — Science and Nature
museum-de-bordeaux-sciences-et-nature.description: Museum born in 1791 from the collection of François-de-Paule Latapie, added to in 1804 by that of the shipowner Bernard Journu-Auber. Housed since 1862 in the Hôtel de Lisleferme, an 18th-century mansion bordering the Jardin Public, it reopened in 2019 after ten years of renovation.

museum-de-grenoble.name: Muséum de Grenoble
museum-de-grenoble.description: Museum founded in 1775 as a cabinet of natural history attached to the public library, and housed since 1855 in a building bordering the Jardin des Plantes. Its collections number around one and a half million specimens of botany, zoology, geology and ethnology, with a strong Alpine component.

museum-de-toulouse.name: Toulouse Natural History Museum
museum-de-toulouse.description: Museum founded in 1865 by the city under the direction of Édouard Filhol, in the former premises of the Discalced Carmelites, occupied as early as 1796 by the naturalist Picot de Lapeyrouse. The first in the world to open a prehistory gallery, it holds more than two and a half million pieces in the Jardin des Plantes.

museum-des-sciences-naturelles-d-angers.name: Angers Natural History Museum
museum-des-sciences-naturelles-d-angers.description: Municipal museum opened to the public in 1801, heir to the cabinet of natural history assembled during the Revolution from collections seized across the Maine-et-Loire. Its holdings comprise around 830,000 objects, including mounted birds, shells, fossils, insects, minerals and hundreds of thousands of herbarium sheets.

museum-henri-lecoq.name: Henri Lecoq Museum
museum-henri-lecoq.description: Museum opened in 1873 in the mansion of the naturalist Henri Lecoq, whose bequest to the city formed the core of the collections. Botany, geology, palaeontology and zoology sit alongside scientific instruments, including a pascaline, the first calculating machine, invented by Blaise Pascal.

museum-national-d-histoire-naturelle.name: National Museum of Natural History
museum-national-d-histoire-naturelle.description: France's national natural history museum, founded in 1793 in the Jardin des Plantes. Its galleries range from the Grande Galerie de l'Évolution to vast collections of paleontology, comparative anatomy, mineralogy and botany.

museum-requien.name: Muséum Requien
museum-requien.description: Avignon's museum of natural history, born from the cabinet assembled in 1840 by the naturalist Esprit Requien, who bequeathed his collections and library to the city. Housed since 1940 in the Hôtel de Raphélis-Soissans, it holds around a million specimens, including the fifth-largest herbarium in France.

musverre.name: Sars-Poteries Glass Museum
musverre.description: Born in 1967 in the former house of the glassworks master, the museum moved in 2016 into a building of blue Hainaut stone by W-Architectures. It holds the largest public collection of contemporary glass in France, more than five hundred works by international artists.

palais-de-l-ile.name: Palais de l'Isle
palais-de-l-ile.description: A former 12th-century fortified house built on an islet in the Thiou, in the heart of Annecy's old town. In turn a lord's residence, a courthouse and a prison, it now offers a tour of the history and heritage of the Annecy basin; courtrooms, cells and a chapel are open to visitors.

palais-des-beaux-arts-de-lille.name: Lille Palais des Beaux-Arts
palais-des-beaux-arts-de-lille.description: Museum founded in 1792 from works confiscated from émigrés and religious institutions, opened to the public in 1809 and then housed in 1892 in a palace built for it on Place de la République. Its collections excel in Flemish and Dutch painting, 19th-century French painting, and fifteen relief maps of towns fortified by Vauban.

palais-du-roure.name: Palais du Roure
palais-du-roure.description: Mansion built in the 15th century for the Florentine Baroncelli family, which Frédéric Mistral nicknamed the 'Palais du Roure' and which became a centre of the Félibrige literary movement. Saved in 1918 by Jeanne de Flandreysy, listed as a historic monument in 1941 and returned to the city in 1944, it holds collections on Mediterranean history and culture.

palais-du-tau-a-reims.name: Palace of Tau, Reims
palais-du-tau-a-reims.description: Former residence of the archbishops of Reims, remodeled in classical style by Robert de Cotte in the late 17th century, the palace hosted the coronation banquets of French kings in its Salle du Tau. A museum since 1972, it displays original statues from the cathedral — including a 5.4-metre Goliath — tapestries, and the coronation treasury, among them Charlemagne's talisman.

palais-galliera-musee-de-la-mode-et-de-l.name: Palais Galliera, Fashion Museum of the City of Paris
palais-galliera-musee-de-la-mode-et-de-l.description: The City of Paris fashion museum, housed in a 19th-century Renaissance-style palace near the Trocadéro. Its collections trace clothing from the 18th century to the present, haute couture included, shown through rotating displays and exhibitions.

palais-jacques-c-ur.name: Palace of Jacques Cœur
palais-jacques-c-ur.description: Residence built between 1443 and 1451 for Jacques Cœur, a wealthy merchant ennobled by Charles VII, in a Flamboyant Gothic style anticipating the Renaissance. Four wings arranged around a courtyard hold carved fireplaces, a chapel decorated with his coat of arms, and eight spiral staircases carved with the shells and hearts that were his emblem.

palais-lascaris.name: Palais Lascaris
palais-lascaris.description: A former aristocratic residence in old Nice, built in the first half of the 17th century by the Lascaris-Vintimille family in the Genoese baroque style. Now a municipal museum, it houses a collection of around 500 antique musical instruments, one of the largest in France.

palais-musee-des-archeveques.name: Archbishops' Palace of Narbonne
palais-musee-des-archeveques.description: A vast archiepiscopal complex combining the Romanesque Palais Vieux and the Gothic Palais Neuf, with its square keep built in 1308 by Archbishop Gilles Aycelin. Listed as a historic monument as early as 1840 and completed in the 19th century with Viollet-le-Duc's neo-Gothic town hall, it houses the museum of art and history and the archaeology museum.

pantheon.name: Panthéon
pantheon.description: A neoclassical monument on the Montagne Sainte-Geneviève, built as a church by Soufflot and turned into the resting place of great French figures — Voltaire, Hugo, Zola and Marie Curie among them. Foucault's pendulum swings beneath its dome.

pavillon-flaubert-a-croisset.name: Pavillon Flaubert
pavillon-flaubert-a-croisset.description: The sole surviving part of the property acquired in 1844 by Gustave Flaubert's father at Croisset, on the banks of the Seine, where the writer lived for thirty-five years and composed his entire body of work. Listed as a historic monument in 1914, the pavilion preserves his writing implements, portraits and personal mementoes, including a gilded Buddha.

pavillon-populaire.name: Pavillon Populaire
pavillon-populaire.description: Neo-Renaissance building constructed in 1891 by the municipal architect Léopold Carlier for the club of the Montpellier students' general association, then handed over to the city's societies, hence its name. Set on the Esplanade Charles-de-Gaulle, it has been an exhibition space devoted to photography since the late 1990s.

petit-palais-musee-des-beaux-arts-de-la-.name: Petit Palais, City of Paris Fine Arts Museum
petit-palais-musee-des-beaux-arts-de-la-.description: Built by Charles Girault for the 1900 World's Fair, the fine arts museum of the City of Paris displays paintings, sculpture and decorative arts from antiquity to 1914 — Rembrandt, Monet and Courbet among them — around a garden courtyard.

pole-d-interpretation-de-la-prehistoire.name: Prehistory Interpretation Centre
pole-d-interpretation-de-la-prehistoire.description: Public institution based in Les Eyzies, at the heart of the Vézère Valley Grand Site de France, whose label it holds and promotes. An information and outreach centre on prehistory, it offers a permanent exhibition, temporary exhibitions, workshops, talks and a media library.

preau-des-accoules-musee-des-enfants.name: Préau des Accoules – Children's Museum
preau-des-accoules-musee-des-enfants.description: A museum designed for children, set on the Montée des Accoules in the covered courtyard of a former Jesuit building in the Panier district, which housed the Marseille observatory from 1702 to 1863. The team designs playful exhibitions drawn from the collections of Marseille's museums to introduce young visitors to works of art.

prieure-du-vieux-logis.name: Prieuré du Vieux Logis
prieure-du-vieux-logis.description: A former mill turned farm, then a priory of the Dominican father Alfred Lemerre, who settled there in 1922 on the Saint-Barthélemy hill. Fitted out as a 15th-century interior and opened as a museum in 1939, it brings together French furniture and objets d'art from the 14th to the 16th century in thirteen rooms.

sainte-chapelle.name: Sainte-Chapelle
sainte-chapelle.description: The Gothic royal chapel on the Île de la Cité, built in the 1240s by Louis IX to house the relics of the Passion. Its upper chapel is ringed by fifteen monumental 13th-century stained-glass windows.

salle-des-mariages-de-l-hotel-de-ville-d.name: Wedding Hall of the Town Hall (Decor by Jean Cocteau)
salle-des-mariages-de-l-hotel-de-ville-d.description: A room in Menton's town hall entirely decorated by Jean Cocteau between 1956 and 1958. The poet painted the myth of Orpheus and Eurydice, a village wedding and a Mediterranean engaged couple, and designed everything down to the chairs, the wrought-iron light fixtures and the leopard-print carpet.

site-archeologique-de-glanum.name: Archaeological Site of Glanum
site-archeologique-de-glanum.description: Ancient city occupied from the 6th century BCE to the 3rd century CE, where a Celto-Ligurian sanctuary built around a healing spring gave way to a Hellenistic settlement influenced by Marseille and then a prosperous Roman town under Augustus. The site preserves a forum, baths, peristyle houses and, at its entrance, the Mausoleum of the Julii and a triumphal arch, together known as Les Antiques.

site-archeologique-de-la-graufesenque.name: La Graufesenque Archaeological Site
site-archeologique-de-la-graufesenque.description: Remains of the Gallo-Roman town of Condatomagus, on the left bank of the Tarn near its confluence with the Dourbie. In the mid-1st century its workshops were the most important centre for the production of terra sigillata ware in the Roman Empire, and its red pottery was distributed throughout the West and far beyond.

site-archeologique-lattara-musee-henri-p.name: Henri Prades Archaeology Museum
site-archeologique-lattara-musee-henri-p.description: Museum opened in 1986 beside the site of Lattara, an ancient port frequented by the Etruscans and Greeks, occupied from the 6th century BC to the Roman period and rediscovered in 1963 by Henri Prades. Ceramics, glassware, metal objects and funerary monuments tell the story of seven centuries of trade in the north-western Mediterranean.

site-des-megalithes-de-locmariaquer.name: Locmariaquer Megaliths
site-des-megalithes-de-locmariaquer.description: Megalithic complex built between 5000 and 3800 BCE, comprising the Grand Menhir Brisé — a granite block over 20 metres long, the largest known standing stone in Europe, now broken into four pieces — the Table des Marchands dolmen and the 140-metre Er Grah tumulus. Inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2025 together with the Carnac megaliths.

site-gallo-romain-de-sanxay.name: Gallo-Roman Site of Sanxay
site-gallo-romain-de-sanxay.description: A vast Gallo-Roman sanctuary devoted to the cult of healing waters, active from the 1st to the 2nd century, centred on a temple with an octagonal cella ringed by a cross-shaped portico, an 89-metre theatre seating close to 6,600 spectators, and a bath complex. Uncovered by Father Camille de La Croix between 1881 and 1883, the sanctuary covers some twenty hectares in the Vonne valley.

site-le-corbusier-firminy.name: Site Le Corbusier Firminy
site-le-corbusier-firminy.description: Urban complex designed by Le Corbusier for the Firminy-Vert district from 1954 onward, at the invitation of the mayor Eugène Claudius-Petit: a house of culture, a stadium, a unité d'habitation housing block and the church of Saint-Pierre. It is the largest ensemble built to his plans in Europe; the church, work on which stopped in 1978, was completed in 2006.

site-memorial-du-camp-des-milles.name: Camp des Milles Memorial Site
site-memorial-du-camp-des-milles.description: A former tile works that became an internment camp in September 1939, where people of thirty-nine nationalities were held, and later an antechamber to Auschwitz as thousands of Jewish men, women and children were deported from it in August and September 1942. The only major French internment and deportation camp to survive intact, it opened as a memorial site in 2012.

sites-et-musee-archeologiques-de-montmau.name: Montmaurin Archaeological Sites and Museum
sites-et-musee-archeologiques-de-montmau.description: The Montmaurin museum traces 400,000 years of human occupation, from the Coupe-Gorge cave — where human remains some 200,000 years old and a cave lion skeleton were unearthed — to the Gallo-Roman villa of Lassalles, a vast agricultural estate transformed in the 4th century into a 5,800-square-metre palace with two peristyles, baths and a hexagonal Gallic temple.

sites-prehistoriques-de-la-vallee-de-la-.name: Prehistoric Sites of the Vézère Valley
sites-prehistoriques-de-la-vallee-de-la-.description: The Centre des monuments nationaux manages seven of the sites inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1979 in the Vézère valley: the decorated caves of Font-de-Gaume and Les Combarelles, the carved Abri du Poisson, the sculpted animal frieze at Cap Blanc, and the Mousterian deposits of Le Moustier, La Micoque and La Ferrassie. Together they document human occupation from the Middle to the Upper Palaeolithic, from Mousterian to Magdalenian times.

tour-pey-berland-a-bordeaux.name: Pey-Berland Tower, Bordeaux
tour-pey-berland-a-bordeaux.description: Gothic bell tower standing apart from Bordeaux's Saint-André Cathedral, built between 1440 and 1500 at the initiative of Archbishop Pey Berland so its bells would not shake the adjoining building. From the top of the 66-metre tower, reached by 233 steps, a panorama opens over Bordeaux; the site is a UNESCO World Heritage listing as part of the Routes of Santiago de Compostela.

tours-de-la-cathedrale-de-reims.name: Towers of Reims Cathedral
tours-de-la-cathedrale-de-reims.description: The western towers of Reims Cathedral, the Gothic building where French kings were crowned from 1027 to 1825 and now a UNESCO World Heritage site, rise about 81.5 metres and were completed around 1275. The climb reaches their summit, past the remains of bells melted in the 1914 fire, for a panorama over the city.

tours-de-la-rochelle.name: Towers of La Rochelle
tours-de-la-rochelle.description: Three medieval towers guard the entrance to La Rochelle's old harbour: the 14th-century Tour Saint-Nicolas and Tour de la Chaîne, once linked by a chain that closed off the port. The Tour de la Lanterne, begun in the late 12th century, later served as a prison for privateers and then for the military; more than 600 graffiti carved by inmates survive inside.

tours-de-notre-dame-de-paris.name: Towers of Notre-Dame de Paris
tours-de-notre-dame-de-paris.description: The medieval towers of Notre-Dame Cathedral, reopened after the post-fire restoration. The climb passes the gallery of chimeras and the belfry of the great bell Emmanuel before reaching a panorama over the Seine and central Paris.

tours-et-remparts-d-aigues-mortes.name: Towers and Ramparts of Aigues-Mortes
tours-et-remparts-d-aigues-mortes.description: The ramparts encircling Aigues-Mortes, 1,640 metres long with 15 towers and 10 gates, were built between 1272 and the late 13th century under Philippe III and then Philippe IV the Fair. The Tour de Constance, built by Saint Louis (Louis IX) between 1240 and 1249, became a prison for Protestant women after 1685; Marie Durand was held there for 38 years, from 1730 to 1768.

tours-et-tresor-de-la-cathedrale-d-amien.name: Towers and Treasury of Amiens Cathedral
tours-et-tresor-de-la-cathedrale-d-amien.description: Amiens Cathedral, begun in 1220 under architect Robert de Luzarches, is the largest Gothic building in France by volume and rises to 112.70 metres; it has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since 1981. The visit climbs 307 steps to the top of the north tower and takes in the treasury, built up since 1206 around the relic of the head of Saint John the Baptist brought back from the Fourth Crusade.

tresor-de-la-cathedrale-d-autun.name: Treasury of Autun Cathedral
tresor-de-la-cathedrale-d-autun.description: Built in the 12th century to house the relics of Saint Lazarus, brought to Autun in 972, Autun Cathedral is renowned for its west tympanum of the Last Judgement, carved by Gislebertus and signed "Gislebertus hoc fecit". Its treasury, housed in a building erected around 1520 by Bishop Jacques Hurault, brings together reliquaries, gold and silver work and liturgical vestments, dispersed during the Revolution and rebuilt as a collection in the 19th century.

tresor-de-la-cathedrale-de-lyon.name: Treasury of Lyon Cathedral
tresor-de-la-cathedrale-de-lyon.description: Lyon's Saint-Jean Cathedral, built between 1175 and 1481 in a style blending Romanesque and Gothic, houses one of the oldest working astronomical clocks, dating from the 14th century. Its treasury, assembled in the 19th century by cardinals Fesch and de Bonald in the adjoining manécanterie, brings together goldwork, Limoges enamels, tapestries and liturgical vestments from the 10th to the 19th century, including a monstrance donated by Joséphine de Beauharnais.

trophee-d-auguste-a-la-turbie.name: Trophy of Augustus at La Turbie
trophee-d-auguste-a-la-turbie.description: Erected in 6 BC on the Via Julia Augusta to celebrate Augustus's subjugation of some fifty Alpine tribes, the Trophy of the Alps originally stood 50 metres tall, with a 38-metre square base topped by a colonnaded rotunda of 24 columns and a conical roof bearing the emperor's statue. Turned into a watchtower in the Middle Ages, the monument was restored in the 1930s with funding from American philanthropist Edward Tuck and reopened in 1934.

vesunna-site-musee-gallo-romain.name: Vesunna, Gallo-Roman Site-Museum
vesunna-site-musee-gallo-romain.description: Museum designed by Jean Nouvel and opened in 2003 above the Domus of Vesunna, a wealthy 1st-century town house excavated from 1959 onward and listed as a historic monument in 1963. Beneath a vast glass canopy can be seen its painted wall coverings, kitchen, private baths and garden with an ornamental pool.

villa-cavrois.name: Villa Cavrois
villa-cavrois.description: Modernist villa built in Croix between 1929 and 1932 by architect Robert Mallet-Stevens for textile magnate Paul Cavrois, its 60-metre length combines reinforced concrete, steel and glass, with a 27-metre swimming pool and materials such as Swedish green marble. Abandoned and vandalised after 1987, listed as a historic monument in 1990, it was acquired by the State and restored before reopening to the public in 2015.

villa-majorelle.name: Villa Majorelle
villa-majorelle.description: A grand house built from 1901 to 1902 for the cabinetmaker Louis Majorelle by the young Parisian architect Henri Sauvage, assisted by Lucien Weissenburger. A centrepiece of the École de Nancy and French Art Nouveau, it combines Majorelle's furniture with paintings by Francis Jourdain and a decor of glazed stoneware.

villa-marguerite-yourcenar.name: Villa Marguerite Yourcenar
villa-marguerite-yourcenar.description: A neo-Norman manor house of the 1930s built on the grounds of the Château Dufresne, destroyed during the First World War, where Marguerite Yourcenar spent her first nine years. Converted in 1997 into a residence for European writers, the villa stands in a forty-hectare departmental park on the Mont Noir.

villa-musee-jean-honore-fragonard.name: Jean-Honoré Fragonard Villa-Museum
villa-musee-jean-honore-fragonard.description: A 17th- and 18th-century bastide in the historic heart of Grasse, once lived in by the painter Jean-Honoré Fragonard and later given to the city by the de Blic family. Its stairwell, decorated with wall paintings, is a listed historic monument; the museum displays works by Fragonard, his son Alexandre-Évariste and Marguerite Gérard.

villa-savoye.name: Villa Savoye
villa-savoye.description: Le Corbusier's modernist villa of 1928–1931 in Poissy, a manifesto of his "five points of architecture" with its pilotis, ribbon windows and roof garden. It is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site.

village-fortifie-mont-dauphin.name: Fortified Village of Mont-Dauphin
village-fortifie-mont-dauphin.description: Fortress town designed by Vauban and built from 1693 on a rocky spur 1,050 metres high, at the confluence of the Guil and Durance valleys, to protect the kingdom from incursions by the Duke of Savoy. Its pink marble ramparts, barracks, sentry turrets, arsenal and powder magazine were inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2008 as part of the Fortifications of Vauban; about 170 people still live in the village.
